title: What are the key labor laws enforced by the UAE Ministry of Labour?
content:
The Ministry of Labour Law UAE, currently known as MOHRE, is the governmental department that is in charge of overseeing employment. Thus, as an employer, it is necessary to learn about the crucial regulations that you should follow to have a compliant workforce.

In this article, you are going to gain a deep insight into the UAE labour laws. Moreover, you will how the Ministry of Labour Law UAE is useful for ensuring smooth employer-employee relationships.

What are the working hours prescribed by the UAE Ministry of Labour?

When you plan to expand to the UAE, you have to take into account several factors. In addition to considering a low-cost business setup in Dubai, you also have to think about the local regulations.

As an employer, you need to follow local employment guidelines to ensure you do not face any issues with the law. And, since working hours are a very important part of employment, you need to follow them.

According to the Ministry of Labour Law UAE, the working hours prescribed are the following:

  • Working hours per day (max): 8 hours
  • Working hours per week (max): 8 hours
  • Employees in hotels, trade, security, and other jobs can work 9 hours but they need approval from the Ministry.
  • Employees under strenuous or harmful work can get a reduction in daily working hours per Ministry decision.
  • Ramadan working hours: during the Holy Month, the working hours get reduced to 6 hours per day.
  • Employees cannot work more than 5 consecutive hours without having a break. Thus, this total rest period should be of an hour or more, no less.

Working hours are a key aspect when calculating salaries. In addition, you need to know about overtime calculation in UAE so you can run an accurate payroll.

How does the UAE Ministry of Labour handle labor disputes?

The Ministry of Labour Law UAE has also established regulations to resolve labour disputes. The current law states the following about disputes:

  • Employees can raise a collective labour dispute against an employer in relation to a joint interest.
  • Employers have to write to the respective labour directorate in case a dispute arises, within the same day.
  • Employees can start a dispute for non-payment of due wages.

According to the law, the steps to follow a dispute are the following:

  • First, there should be a direct negotiation.
  • If the dispute is not solved, then the labour directorate can mediate between both parties.
  • If it is not solved, the competent reconciliation committee will act.
  • Lastly, if the dispute is not solved, then arbitration follows to reach a settlement.

What are the rights of employees under UAE labour laws?

The UAE is a place known for welcoming people from different backgrounds who want to work and live in their thriving cities. In this regard, given that employment relations tend to be difficult, the Ministry of Labour Law UAE helps individuals exercise their rights.

Employees in the UAE have rights to the following:

  • 8 working hours per day or 48 hours per week
  • Paid overtime hours
  • Breaks for rest, meals and prayer.
  • Weekly rest day fully paid.
  • Public holidays
  • Annual leave
  • Bereavement leave
  • Parental leave and maternity leave
  • Study leave
  • Labour complaints

Employees have also the right to use ICA Smart Services Dubai, so they can check different documentation such as visa status or residence status.

How can employers and employees stay informed about UAE labour laws?

Regardless if your company is in the Fujairah Free Zone or any other Emirate or Free Zone, you still have to comply with the Ministry of Labour law UAE.

Since the law in the UAE changes constantly, as an employer, you can stay informed by doing the following:

  • Instruct a team of your HR staff to stay always up-to-date with the changes
  • Hire expert lawyers to work for your company to help you simplify legal procedures
  • Contact a service provider that can ensure total compliance

In the case of employees, you also have to be informed regarding the change in regulations, as you need to know your rights. Make sure to check the MOHRE website and read the law.

Where can I lodge a complaint or seek assistance regarding labour issues in the UAE?

In the case an employee wants to submit a complaint, they have to act immediately, within 30 days of the employer’s breach. For instance, if you have a complaint about gratuity law in UAE, you need to know how to file it.

In this case, the worker has the following options:

  • Call the Ministry of Labour Dubai contact number through the Labor Claims and Advisory Center to get advice on how to proceed.
  • Submit a complaint through the MOHRE portal

According to the Ministry, they can solve the dispute in a range of 14 working days or less. Thus, the goal is to reach an amicable settlement, while always protecting worker’s and employer’s rights.

What are the Ministry of Labour Dubai timings?

The Ministry of Labour Dubai timings are the following:

  • Monday to Thursday: From 7:30 am until 3:30 pm
  • Friday: From 7: 30 am until 12:00 pm

During Saturdays and Sundays, the Ministry does not work. Thus, as an employer, you need to organize what you need to do since on weekends you cannot go in person to the Ministry.

However, the call centre and online services are 24/7 so you can submit your queries and carry out your services through the official site without any issue.

Is there a toll-free number to contact the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

To contact the Ministry of Labour Law UAE you can use any of the 13 channels available, including the Ministry of Labour Dubai toll free number. The call centre allows you to solve your doubts and enquiries related to MOHRE and it is available in 20 languages for your comfort.

How can I check the status of my work permit with the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

You can check the status of your work permit easily by entering the MOHRE Portal. You just have to go through the following basic steps:

  • Visit the official MOHRE website
  • Look for “New Enquiry Service” which is under the “Services” tab in the main menu.
  • On the search bar, enter the words “work permit” to find the service you want to check.
  • Provide the requested information
  • Click on search, and immediately you will see the status of your work permit.

What is the contact number for the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

You can call the Ministry of Labour Law UAE through their local or international call centre, and the numbers are the following:

  • Call center: 600590000
  • International call center: 0091-7168027666

What role does the Ministry of Labour play in the business formation process?

During company formation, employers must follow all the guidelines and steps established so they can ensure a smooth incorporation. While the employer is planning to register the company, they should consider the company size based on the number of employees they want to hire.

This is because the company has to get an employee quota approval from MOHRE. This refers to the maximum number of employees the company can hire. So, MOHRE plays a crucial role according to how large you want your workforce to be.

What labor regulations are enforced by the MOL during business formation?

The Ministry of Labour Law UAE is the governing body of employment, and as such, it contains all the regulations that companies must follow when considering business formation.

Once your company has been registered, you have to do the following:

  • Apply for an establishment card
  • Register at the General Directorate of Residency and Foreign affairs

By following these two steps you are ensuring your company is ready to hire employees. And, for each employee, you are obliged to apply for a labour card at MOHRE.

How does the MOL impact the hiring process for businesses?

During the hiring process, employers have to apply for a UAE Employment Visa for their employees once they know they are the perfect fit for the position.

However, before hiring the candidate, employers have to follow the regulations established by the Ministry of Labour Dubai. It is necessary to do the following:

  • Submit a signed contract, both in Arabic and English. The contract should be in accordance with MOHRE’s format.
  • Apply for a labour card (work permit) at MOHRE so the employee is allowed to work legally in the UAE.
  • Obtain the entry permit after the pre-approval of the work permit.

In addition, the Emiratisation policy also affects the hiring process. Companies should aim to hire a diverse workforce and include a percentage of Emiratis.

What resources does the MOL offer to assist businesses with compliance?

On the MOHRE website, there is an entire section with information regarding Laws & Regulations. Here, businesses can check all the laws issued by the Ministry so they can ensure compliance.

In addition, users get access to Ministerial Resolutions and FAQs, and they can also contact MOHRE directly to solve their doubts regarding non-compliance.

What happens if a business fails to comply with labor regulations enforced by the MOL?

Employers have to comply with the regulations established by MOHRE, otherwise, they can be subject to fines and penalties. For instance, you have to comply with the UAE establishment card.

But if you fail to renew it, the fine can range from AED 500 to AED 2000. Other fines may be the following:

  • Non-payment of salaries to workers: fine from AED 3,000-10,000 and imprisonment for 6 months.
  • Not cancelling the work permit: AED 1000 fine, and imprisonment for 3 months.
  • Failure to report an occupational accident: AED 3000-10,000 fine plus 6 months of imprisonment.

Establishing a business in the UAE involves learning everything about the Ministry of Labour Law UAE so you can stay in compliance. We understand how complex can be to incorporate a company as well as to understand the law.

For this reason, we want to offer you our support so you can have a smooth incorporation in the UAE. Contact us to learn why our team can be the best solution for starting your business in the UAE.

In this article, you are going to gain a deep insight into the UAE labour laws. Moreover, you will how the Ministry of Labour Law UAE is useful for ensuring smooth employer-employee relationships.

What are the working hours prescribed by the UAE Ministry of Labour?

When you plan to expand to the UAE, you have to take into account several factors. In addition to considering a low-cost business setup in Dubai, you also have to think about the local regulations.

As an employer, you need to follow local employment guidelines to ensure you do not face any issues with the law. And, since working hours are a very important part of employment, you need to follow them.

According to the Ministry of Labour Law UAE, the working hours prescribed are the following:

  • Working hours per day (max): 8 hours
  • Working hours per week (max): 8 hours
  • Employees in hotels, trade, security, and other jobs can work 9 hours but they need approval from the Ministry.
  • Employees under strenuous or harmful work can get a reduction in daily working hours per Ministry decision.
  • Ramadan working hours: during the Holy Month, the working hours get reduced to 6 hours per day.
  • Employees cannot work more than 5 consecutive hours without having a break. Thus, this total rest period should be of an hour or more, no less.

Working hours are a key aspect when calculating salaries. In addition, you need to know about overtime calculation in UAE so you can run an accurate payroll.

How does the UAE Ministry of Labour handle labor disputes?

The Ministry of Labour Law UAE has also established regulations to resolve labour disputes. The current law states the following about disputes:

  • Employees can raise a collective labour dispute against an employer in relation to a joint interest.
  • Employers have to write to the respective labour directorate in case a dispute arises, within the same day.
  • Employees can start a dispute for non-payment of due wages.

According to the law, the steps to follow a dispute are the following:

  • First, there should be a direct negotiation.
  • If the dispute is not solved, then the labour directorate can mediate between both parties.
  • If it is not solved, the competent reconciliation committee will act.
  • Lastly, if the dispute is not solved, then arbitration follows to reach a settlement.

What are the rights of employees under UAE labour laws?

The UAE is a place known for welcoming people from different backgrounds who want to work and live in their thriving cities. In this regard, given that employment relations tend to be difficult, the Ministry of Labour Law UAE helps individuals exercise their rights.

Employees in the UAE have rights to the following:

  • 8 working hours per day or 48 hours per week
  • Paid overtime hours
  • Breaks for rest, meals and prayer.
  • Weekly rest day fully paid.
  • Public holidays
  • Annual leave
  • Bereavement leave
  • Parental leave and maternity leave
  • Study leave
  • Labour complaints

Employees have also the right to use ICA Smart Services Dubai, so they can check different documentation such as visa status or residence status.

How can employers and employees stay informed about UAE labour laws?

Regardless if your company is in the Fujairah Free Zone or any other Emirate or Free Zone, you still have to comply with the Ministry of Labour law UAE.

Since the law in the UAE changes constantly, as an employer, you can stay informed by doing the following:

  • Instruct a team of your HR staff to stay always up-to-date with the changes
  • Hire expert lawyers to work for your company to help you simplify legal procedures
  • Contact a service provider that can ensure total compliance

In the case of employees, you also have to be informed regarding the change in regulations, as you need to know your rights. Make sure to check the MOHRE website and read the law.

Where can I lodge a complaint or seek assistance regarding labour issues in the UAE?

In the case an employee wants to submit a complaint, they have to act immediately, within 30 days of the employer’s breach. For instance, if you have a complaint about gratuity law in UAE, you need to know how to file it.

In this case, the worker has the following options:

  • Call the Ministry of Labour Dubai contact number through the Labor Claims and Advisory Center to get advice on how to proceed.
  • Submit a complaint through the MOHRE portal

According to the Ministry, they can solve the dispute in a range of 14 working days or less. Thus, the goal is to reach an amicable settlement, while always protecting worker’s and employer’s rights.

What are the Ministry of Labour Dubai timings?

The Ministry of Labour Dubai timings are the following:

  • Monday to Thursday: From 7:30 am until 3:30 pm
  • Friday: From 7: 30 am until 12:00 pm

During Saturdays and Sundays, the Ministry does not work. Thus, as an employer, you need to organize what you need to do since on weekends you cannot go in person to the Ministry.

However, the call centre and online services are 24/7 so you can submit your queries and carry out your services through the official site without any issue.

Is there a toll-free number to contact the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

To contact the Ministry of Labour Law UAE you can use any of the 13 channels available, including the Ministry of Labour Dubai toll free number. The call centre allows you to solve your doubts and enquiries related to MOHRE and it is available in 20 languages for your comfort.

How can I check the status of my work permit with the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

You can check the status of your work permit easily by entering the MOHRE Portal. You just have to go through the following basic steps:

  • Visit the official MOHRE website
  • Look for “New Enquiry Service” which is under the “Services” tab in the main menu.
  • On the search bar, enter the words “work permit” to find the service you want to check.
  • Provide the requested information
  • Click on search, and immediately you will see the status of your work permit.

What is the contact number for the Ministry of Labour Dubai?

You can call the Ministry of Labour Law UAE through their local or international call centre, and the numbers are the following:

  • Call center: 600590000
  • International call center: 0091-7168027666

What role does the Ministry of Labour play in the business formation process?

During company formation, employers must follow all the guidelines and steps established so they can ensure a smooth incorporation. While the employer is planning to register the company, they should consider the company size based on the number of employees they want to hire.

This is because the company has to get an employee quota approval from MOHRE. This refers to the maximum number of employees the company can hire. So, MOHRE plays a crucial role according to how large you want your workforce to be.

What labor regulations are enforced by the MOL during business formation?

The Ministry of Labour Law UAE is the governing body of employment, and as such, it contains all the regulations that companies must follow when considering business formation.

Once your company has been registered, you have to do the following:

  • Apply for an establishment card
  • Register at the General Directorate of Residency and Foreign affairs

By following these two steps you are ensuring your company is ready to hire employees. And, for each employee, you are obliged to apply for a labour card at MOHRE.

How does the MOL impact the hiring process for businesses?

During the hiring process, employers have to apply for a UAE Employment Visa for their employees once they know they are the perfect fit for the position.

However, before hiring the candidate, employers have to follow the regulations established by the Ministry of Labour Dubai. It is necessary to do the following:

  • Submit a signed contract, both in Arabic and English. The contract should be in accordance with MOHRE’s format.
  • Apply for a labour card (work permit) at MOHRE so the employee is allowed to work legally in the UAE.
  • Obtain the entry permit after the pre-approval of the work permit.

In addition, the Emiratisation policy also affects the hiring process. Companies should aim to hire a diverse workforce and include a percentage of Emiratis.

What resources does the MOL offer to assist businesses with compliance?

On the MOHRE website, there is an entire section with information regarding Laws & Regulations. Here, businesses can check all the laws issued by the Ministry so they can ensure compliance.

In addition, users get access to Ministerial Resolutions and FAQs, and they can also contact MOHRE directly to solve their doubts regarding non-compliance.

What happens if a business fails to comply with labor regulations enforced by the MOL?

Employers have to comply with the regulations established by MOHRE, otherwise, they can be subject to fines and penalties. For instance, you have to comply with the UAE establishment card.

But if you fail to renew it, the fine can range from AED 500 to AED 2000. Other fines may be the following:

  • Non-payment of salaries to workers: fine from AED 3,000-10,000 and imprisonment for 6 months.
  • Not cancelling the work permit: AED 1000 fine, and imprisonment for 3 months.
  • Failure to report an occupational accident: AED 3000-10,000 fine plus 6 months of imprisonment.

Establishing a business in the UAE involves learning everything about the Ministry of Labour Law UAE so you can stay in compliance. We understand how complex can be to incorporate a company as well as to understand the law.

For this reason, we want to offer you our support so you can have a smooth incorporation in the UAE. Contact us to learn why our team can be the best solution for starting your business in the UAE.

title: Check MOHRE Work Permit Status UAE | Fast & Easy
content:
UAE doesn’t do anything slow. Everything, from metro rides to ministry approvals, moves at breakneck speed. So if you’re stuck wondering about your MoHRE work permit status, you’re already behind. But you don’t need to be!

In a country where rules move fast and fines move faster, knowing your permit status is basic self-preservation. Whether you’re waiting on approval, tracking renewals, or sorting out a temporary work permit MoHRE issued, this blog post will show you exactly how to check it fast. And yes, it actually is easy.

Even better? Once you know how to do it yourself, you don’t need to rely on someone else or wonder where your paperwork is lost in the digital void. You get answers on your terms.

Key Takeaways: How to Check Your MOHRE Work Permit Status

  • Use the MOHRE website or app
  • Keep your application number ready
  • Know what each status means
  • Follow up if anything looks off
  • Check it weekly for peace of mind
  • Let free zone services manage it for you
  • Don’t wait for your employer to keep you informed

What Exactly is a MOHRE Work Permit?

Your dream job is right there, but a little digital status holds the key. We get it. Waiting for official confirmation feels like watching paint dry. But what if you didn’t have to just… wait? What if you could peek behind the curtain anytime?

Think of it as your official UAE government stamp of approval to work for a specific employer. Issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE), it’s non-negotiable for most private sector jobs outside free zones. No permit, no legal employment. Simple as that.

  • It’s linked to your employer: Your sponsor (employer) applies for it on your behalf.
  • It has a validity period: Usually 1 to 2 years and it’s totally renewable.
  • It’s your legal shield: Proof you’re authorized to work, protecting your rights.

Why Bother Checking Your MoHRE Work Permit Status? 

Knowing where things stand is practical power:

  • No more pestering HR daily. You can get the answers directly.
  • See the section of Approved. Start packing, booking flights, and giving notice back home.
  • If it is Rejected or needs action, you know now, instead of weeks later.
  • Confirm validity dates so you are never caught off guard near renewal time.

Your Fast Track: How to Check MOHRE Work Permit Status

Forget long queues or phone calls. UAE’s government has smartly moved this process online. Here are your main routes:

Option 1: The MOHRE Website

This is the official source, straight from the source.

  1. Head Here: Go to the official MOHRE website: mohre.gov.ae.
  2. Find the Service: Look for Services or E-Services in the main menu. Head to the Work Permit Services.
  3. Choose Inquiry. Select the option for Work Permit Inquiry or Application Status Inquiry.
  4. Enter your details. You will likely need your application number that’s provided by your employer and your passport number.
  5. Hit the inquiry button. Your current MoHRE work permit status will display clearly.

Option 2: The MOHRE App

Prefer your phone? The official MOHRE app, that’s available on iOS & Android, puts the info in your pocket.

  1. Search MOHRE UAE in your app store. Download and install.
  2. Create an account or log in if you have one. You might need your UAE Pass for full access.
  3. Find the Services or Inquiries section within the app.
  4. Select Permit Inquiry. Look for Work Permit Status or Application Inquiry.
  5. Input Info: Enter your Application Number and Passport Number.
  6. Instant Result: Your permit status pops up instantly.

Option 3: Tas’heel Service Centers

Prefer face-to-face? Or maybe you’re encountering online glitches? Visit a Tas’heel service center.

  1. Find Your nearest center. Check the MOHRE website for Tas’heel locations and operating hours.
  2. Take your documents with you. Bring your passport and any application reference number you have.
  3. Ask the staff. Request an update on your work permit application status. They can access the system.

What Do Status Messages Really Mean?

Seeing a status but unsure? Here’s what they mean:

1. Under Process/Application Received:

It’s in the queue. Check back in a day or two.

2. Approved:

Congratulations! Your MOHRE work permit is official. Next steps like entry permit or visa should follow soon.

3. Rejected:

Don’t panic immediately. There’s usually a reason stated such as a missing document or info mismatch. Your employer needs to address it and potentially reapply. Ask them for details.

4. Cancelled:

The application was withdrawn, usually by the employer. Clarify with them why.

5. Expired:

Time’s up! Renewal is needed before you can legally continue working.

Issued: Similar to Approved. You are good to go!

Why You Should Check Regularly:

Like all tech systems, the MOHRE database isn’t foolproof. Glitches happen. Statuses get stuck. Check your MoHRE work permit status every week if:

  • You’re changing jobs
  • You’re on a short-term contract
  • Your employer is “delayed” with paperwork
  • You’re unsure if your visa process has started
  • You’re facing salary issues or delays
  • You plan to travel and need to confirm work permit validity

Who Actually Applies for the Work Permit?

It’s your employer. But that doesn’t mean you stay clueless. Always follow up once your employer confirms submission. Ask for the application number and don’t hesitate to do your own checks. It shows initiative and prevents surprises.

If you are moving between employers, always confirm that your old permit is cancelled before the new one is applied.

Can You Speed Up the Process?

Not really. The only way to avoid delays is by making sure your documents are in order before submission. That means:

  • A valid passport
  • Clean record (no immigration bans)
  • Medical tests done
  • Accurate employer records
  • No duplicate permit requests in process

If you’re using a free zone service like ours, we handle all this from the jump. We precheck your documents, handle submission, and keep you updated throughout.

Troubleshooting Common Status Check Issues

Technology is wonderful… until it isn’t. If things go sideways:

“No Record Found”

Triple-check your Application Number and Passport Number. Make sure your employer actually submitted it. If confirmed correct, wait 24 hours – sometimes system sync lags. Still nothing? Employer needs to follow up.

Website or App is Down

Try again later. Government portals occasionally have maintenance. Check MOHRE social media for outage notices.

Status Stuck on “Under Process” for Ages

MOHRE aims for 5 working days for standard permits. If it’s way beyond that, your employer should contact MOHRE directly to inquire. Delays can happen if additional checks are needed.

Forgot Application Number?

You need this. Contact your employer’s PRO or HR department immediately. They hold the keys.

What About Temporary Permits?

Need someone for a short, urgent project? The temporary work permit MoHRE offers a solution that’s usually valid for up to 3 months. Checking its status follows the exact same methods above! Use the application number provided for that specific temporary permit.

Beyond the Status of Your Permit:

Knowing your status is step one. Keep things smooth:

Renewal Reminders:

Don’t wait for expiry panic! Set reminders 2-3 months before your permit ends. Your employer handles renewal, but stay informed.

Job Change?

Your permit is tied to your employer. Changing jobs means a new permit application. Don’t start the new role until the new permit is approved!

Lost Permit?

Report it immediately to your employer and MOHRE. A replacement can be issued.

Feeling overwhelmed by the process itself, not just the status check? While getting the status is easy, managing the entire work permit application can be complex.

If your company needs support with UAE licensing or work permits, check out our expert UAE licensing services designed to make setup smooth. Let us handle the paperwork, so you can focus on the people.

Conclusion:

Waiting for your MOHRE work permit doesn’t have to be a black hole of anxiety. Armed with the right info, your application number, passport, and knowing where to look, you can check your MoHRE work permit status in minutes, anytime.

Whether you prefer the website, the app, or a service center, transparency is built into the system. Use that power. Track your progress. Plan your move. And step into your new UAE role with confidence, knowing your paperwork is squared away. Now go chase that opportunity!

Your MOHRE Work Permit Status FAQs with Quick Answers:

Q: How long does it take to get a MOHRE work permit approved?

A: MOHRE typically processes standard applications within 5 working days. Complex cases or requests for additional info can take longer.

Q: Can I check the status without the application number?

A: Realistically, no. The application number is essential for online and app inquiries. Always get this from your employer immediately after they apply.

Q: My status says “Rejected.” What now?

A: Contact your employer’s HR or your PRO immediately. They will receive the specific reason for rejection and can advise on the next steps.

Q: Does checking the status myself affect the application?

A: Absolutely not! Checking your status is purely an inquiry. It doesn’t slow down or impact the processing in any way.

Q: What’s the difference between a work permit and a residence visa?

A: The MOHRE work permit authorizes you to work for a specific employer. The residence visa (issued by immigration – ICP/GDRFA) allows you to live in the UAE. You usually need the work permit approved first before applying for the residence visa.

Q: My employer is in a Free Zone. Does this apply?

A: Free Zones often issue their own work permits. If your employer is specifically in a Free Zone (like DIFC, DMCC, ADGM, JAFZA, etc.), check their respective portal for permit status. MOHRE handles the mainland and some specific sectors.

title: Guide for Moving to Dubai From UK with Freelance Visa
content:
If you are contemplating the exciting prospect of moving to Dubai from UK, you are embarking on an adventure like no other. Dubai, situated in the heart of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), is a city of remarkable contrasts, where tradition meets innovation, and limitless opportunities await.The allure of Dubai lies in its luxurious lifestyle and the promise of a thriving career and a quality of life.

In this article, we will equip you with the knowledge to navigate this transformative journey seamlessly. We will delve into the benefits of calling Dubai your new home, dissect the visa requirements essential for your move. Overall, we will explore the crucial documentation process. So, let us ensure you have everything you need to embark on this exciting chapter of your life.

Benefits of Living in Dubai UAE

Are you contemplating moving to Dubai from UK? Dubai offers a wealth of compelling reasons to make this exciting transition. From stunning skyscrapers to a diverse cultural scene, Dubai’s allure is undeniable.

Move to Dubai from UK and experience a tax-free income environment. This financial advantage alone can significantly boost your quality of life. Moreover, Dubai’s dynamic job market is brimming with opportunities across various industries.

When moving from UK to Dubai, you will find a cosmopolitan city that respects diversity. Dubai’s inclusive society encourages individuals from various backgrounds to thrive, making it an ideal place for relocation.

Relocating to Dubai from UK opens doors to a world of experiences. You can enjoy the bustling markets, world-class dining, and unparalleled shopping. The city’s excellent healthcare and education systems ensure your family’s well-being and growth.

Moving to UAE from UK means embracing a vibrant lifestyle. Dubai’s warm climate allows for outdoor activities year-round, from beach days to desert adventures. The city’s safety and efficient public services provide peace of mind.

So, to answer the question “Can I move to Dubai from UK?”. Yes, you can! With the right visa, like the Dubai freelance visa, your dream of a new life in the UAE is well within reach. Dubai’s unique blend of modernity and tradition awaits your exploration.

Visa Requirements for Moving to Dubai from UK

When contemplating moving to Dubai from UK, understanding the visa requirements is paramount. Dubai’s visa system is well-defined and offers various options to cater to your specific needs.

In short, moving to Dubai from UK involves understanding the diverse visa options available, such as the Dubai freelance visa and Retirement Visa, and securing a sponsor for your application. This careful planning will help ensure a smooth transition to your new life in Dubai.

In this section, we will explore the different visas available for UK residents planning to make the move, including the coveted freelance visa Dubai.

Legal and Visa Considerations When Moving from UK to Dubai

content:
Legal documents are vital for getting hired or setting up a company in a specific business location. These elements allow individuals to reach their goals in a legal way, and it also brings benefits to them. But in this case, we will focus on one specific document; the NOC in UAE. If you want to work or set up in the UAE, you must learn about this document.

In this article, you will learn all you need to know about the NOC letter Dubai and everything it involves. For instance, here you can find information about its importance and how it works, which will help you understand better. Also, you will be able to find relevant information about the process to obtain it. Let’s observe:

What is the NOC letter in Dubai, UAE and why is it important?

In case you’re not aware of what is NOC in Dubai, UAE, here we will show you everything about it. First of all, you must know that it is a legal document known as a No Objection Certificate. However, it is commonly known by its acronyms NOC in many countries, including the UAE.

Normally, an organization or an individual can issue this type of legal document for one main reason. The main function of it is letting know that there are no objections to the points made within the document. Nonetheless, it is only a requirement that is necessary when purchasing a property in the UAE.

In that case, the developer needs to give a clear title on the purchased property by using the NOC. Besides, it will help them show that all the service changes and utilities have been paid too. In other words, it proves that there’s no objection from the developer to another individual buying the property.

Although you now know the basic information about the NOC in UAE, you should learn more about it. For example, you should learn about its content and how to obtain it in some other cases too. Therefore, keep reading this article to discover all the information you need to know about this document.

Does the NOC letter allow employees to work in another country?

The answer is yes; all employees have the opportunity to travel to another country for work purposes. Nonetheless, it will be necessary to obtain a No Objection Certificate letter from their employer or sponsor. Certainly, the process to obtain this document must be done before they leave their home country.

You should also know that this letter is usually written by the employer of the HR department of the company. However, that is in case the employee has already applied for a visa. On the other hand, if you’re an employee, it’s also possible to request a NOC from your boss or manager.

As a tip, you should have a clear idea regarding the duration of your stay in the other country. Keeping that in mind, you will be able to manage your time and workload properly. Besides, it will also allow you to return to your home country without having any problems.

Can employees work for two employers at the same time in the UAE?

Employees can get two jobs in the UAE; the main one (full-time job), and the secondary one (part-time job). However, the UAE labor law has strict rules regarding this matter and you should know about them. For example, if an employee desired to have two jobs, they needed a NOC letter to work in other company.

Nonetheless, these rules have been modified during the last few years to make them more flexible. In fact, the MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation) introduced a new system for this process. This new system allows employees to have many part-time jobs now without requiring approval from their main employer.

Nonetheless, a NOC letter from their sponsor is necessary in case they are in the country on a family visa. After obtaining a No Objection Certificate, they must submit it to the MOHRE to apply for a part-time work permit.

Is it Necessary to provide a NOC letter to apply for a visa?

It is not a requirement to provide a No Objection Certificate to apply for a visa in the UAE. However, there is a specific type of visa that actually requires it during the application process. The type of visa that requires a NOC in UAE is the Schengen Visa. You’d probably desire to know about this document.

The Schengen Visa has the main function that is allowing an individual to travel to another country. Although this document will allow the person to travel as a tourist, it will have other functions. For instance, it will help them to fulfill their reason for visit, which can be academic, official, or vacation time.

Who can apply for this type of visa in the UAE?

There are two main categories of people who can apply for a Schengen Visa in the UAE. Those are the following ones:

  • Individuals who hold UAE passports and have been previously refused visa-free entry to the Schengen area.
  • Foreigners who live in the UAE by using a temporary or permanent residence permit. These should be nationals of a country that already has an agreement on a visa-free regime with Schengen. Another valid case is that these foreigners are from a country that doesn’t have a visa-free regime with Schengen.

How can you complete the process to get a NOC letter?

There are methods to get a No Objection letter from sponsor to work for visa purposes mostly. However, these methods can vary according to the type of business where the applicant works. Let’s take a look at the basic method’s steps you should follow to obtain this document:

  • The first step consists of seeking permission from your sponsor or employer to take time off for visa purposes. This should be during the time span in which you plan to visit the other country.
  • After that, you will receive the required approval. And once you have received it, you can write your NOC letter. Remember that you can also have a professional coworker who can write your letter of no opposition.

What are the key elements that a basic NOC letter must contain?

If you want to learn to create a draft of a NOC in UAE, here’s how you should do it. Follow this example of a basic format to create this document:

  • Firstly, it is essential to mention the date at the beginning of the NOC document.
  • In order to show the authenticity of your NOC, it should be on an official letter head.
  • After that, it should mention the applicant’s name below. Keep in mind that it must spell the name exactly like in the verification identities of the applicant.
  • It also must indicate the applicant’s designation that he/she holds in the organization prior to applying for the visa.
  • It must show the amount of salary that the applicant receives in the company prior to applying for the visa.
  • Also, it should mention the date of joining on which the applicant wants to start operating in the company.
  • A vital element that the NOC must contain is a genuine reason for the procurement of a visa for the other country. Therefore, in this section, the applicant must be precise when describing the reason why he/she needs the visa.
  • Besides, the document must mention the contact details of the Human Resources department. This is in case the applicant was working prior to filling for a visa.
  • It should also mention the designation of the NOC approving officer.
  • The NOC also has to indicate the address of the company the applicant seeks to procure the visa for.
  • And lastly, it must include the date of the validity of the document. This detail denotes the duration of the applicant until which he/she can operate in another country.

How can you apply for a part-time work permit in the UAE?

On the other hand, if you want to obtain a part-time work permit, you will need a NOC in UAE. This type of permit can bring you many benefits, such as getting extra income, experience, and skills. Nonetheless, you should learn how to apply for this permit before obtaining a part-time job.

Firstly, you should know that you get this special permit from the MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources & Emiratisation). Besides, it is important to be aware of its duration and the fees it requires. A part-time work permit is only valid for one year, and your part-time employer must pay an AED 600 fee.

This cost consists of two main fees, which are the application fee (AED 100) and the approval fee (AED 500). Another important detail that must be considered is the consequences of working for another company without a work permit. In this case, the hiring company or organization must face a fine of AED 50,000.

In order to apply for this permit, you will need these documents:

  • A passport copy.
  • A colored photograph of the applicant.
  • NOC letter from sponsor (if applicable).
  • A copy of the business’s trade licenses.
  • Copy of the residency visa.
  • A copy of the new work contract.
  • Relevant academic qualifications.
  • A letter of approval from the pertinent authorities.

How can Connectfz help you obtain more information about the NOC in the UAE?

As you can see, the NOC in UAE is necessary in order to work in the country or abroad. Besides, it is also useful when applying for a specific visa or purchasing a property in the UAE. Therefore, you should request consultancy services in case you need help to obtain your NOC letter.

Working with Connectfz by your side is your best chance to obtain what you need and fulfill your requirements. The main reason for this is that you will be able to follow professional tips and advice. Besides, you can also learn about the business setup process in case you want to build your own company.

However, if you have already built your business, you can make it more efficient with support services. For example, requesting recruitment services is the best option to find and hire the employees you need. Other services you might need are staff outsourcing, tax advisory, payroll, visa services, and many others.

Would you like to contact Connectfz to obtain more relevant information that you may need about the NOC (No Objection Certificate) in the UAE? If you have any questions, call us on +97143316688. You can email us at info@connectfz.ae, and you will talk to one of our representatives who will answer your questions.

Although you now know the basic information about the NOC in UAE, you should learn more about it. For example, you should learn about its content and how to obtain it in some other cases too. Therefore, keep reading this article to discover all the information you need to know about this document.

Does the NOC letter allow employees to work in another country?

The answer is yes; all employees have the opportunity to travel to another country for work purposes. Nonetheless, it will be necessary to obtain a No Objection Certificate letter from their employer or sponsor. Certainly, the process to obtain this document must be done before they leave their home country.

You should also know that this letter is usually written by the employer of the HR department of the company. However, that is in case the employee has already applied for a visa. On the other hand, if you’re an employee, it’s also possible to request a NOC from your boss or manager.

As a tip, you should have a clear idea regarding the duration of your stay in the other country. Keeping that in mind, you will be able to manage your time and workload properly. Besides, it will also allow you to return to your home country without having any problems.

Can employees work for two employers at the same time in the UAE?

Employees can get two jobs in the UAE; the main one (full-time job), and the secondary one (part-time job). However, the UAE labor law has strict rules regarding this matter and you should know about them. For example, if an employee desired to have two jobs, they needed a NOC letter to work in other company.

Nonetheless, these rules have been modified during the last few years to make them more flexible. In fact, the MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation) introduced a new system for this process. This new system allows employees to have many part-time jobs now without requiring approval from their main employer.

Nonetheless, a NOC letter from their sponsor is necessary in case they are in the country on a family visa. After obtaining a No Objection Certificate, they must submit it to the MOHRE to apply for a part-time work permit.

Is it Necessary to provide a NOC letter to apply for a visa?

It is not a requirement to provide a No Objection Certificate to apply for a visa in the UAE. However, there is a specific type of visa that actually requires it during the application process. The type of visa that requires a NOC in UAE is the Schengen Visa. You’d probably desire to know about this document.

The Schengen Visa has the main function that is allowing an individual to travel to another country. Although this document will allow the person to travel as a tourist, it will have other functions. For instance, it will help them to fulfill their reason for visit, which can be academic, official, or vacation time.

Who can apply for this type of visa in the UAE?

There are two main categories of people who can apply for a Schengen Visa in the UAE. Those are the following ones:

  • Individuals who hold UAE passports and have been previously refused visa-free entry to the Schengen area.
  • Foreigners who live in the UAE by using a temporary or permanent residence permit. These should be nationals of a country that already has an agreement on a visa-free regime with Schengen. Another valid case is that these foreigners are from a country that doesn’t have a visa-free regime with Schengen.

How can you complete the process to get a NOC letter?

There are methods to get a No Objection letter from sponsor to work for visa purposes mostly. However, these methods can vary according to the type of business where the applicant works. Let’s take a look at the basic method’s steps you should follow to obtain this document:

  • The first step consists of seeking permission from your sponsor or employer to take time off for visa purposes. This should be during the time span in which you plan to visit the other country.
  • After that, you will receive the required approval. And once you have received it, you can write your NOC letter. Remember that you can also have a professional coworker who can write your letter of no opposition.

What are the key elements that a basic NOC letter must contain?

If you want to learn to create a draft of a NOC in UAE, here’s how you should do it. Follow this example of a basic format to create this document:

  • Firstly, it is essential to mention the date at the beginning of the NOC document.
  • In order to show the authenticity of your NOC, it should be on an official letter head.
  • After that, it should mention the applicant’s name below. Keep in mind that it must spell the name exactly like in the verification identities of the applicant.
  • It also must indicate the applicant’s designation that he/she holds in the organization prior to applying for the visa.
  • It must show the amount of salary that the applicant receives in the company prior to applying for the visa.
  • Also, it should mention the date of joining on which the applicant wants to start operating in the company.
  • A vital element that the NOC must contain is a genuine reason for the procurement of a visa for the other country. Therefore, in this section, the applicant must be precise when describing the reason why he/she needs the visa.
  • Besides, the document must mention the contact details of the Human Resources department. This is in case the applicant was working prior to filling for a visa.
  • It should also mention the designation of the NOC approving officer.
  • The NOC also has to indicate the address of the company the applicant seeks to procure the visa for.
  • And lastly, it must include the date of the validity of the document. This detail denotes the duration of the applicant until which he/she can operate in another country.

How can you apply for a part-time work permit in the UAE?

On the other hand, if you want to obtain a part-time work permit, you will need a NOC in UAE. This type of permit can bring you many benefits, such as getting extra income, experience, and skills. Nonetheless, you should learn how to apply for this permit before obtaining a part-time job.

Firstly, you should know that you get this special permit from the MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources & Emiratisation). Besides, it is important to be aware of its duration and the fees it requires. A part-time work permit is only valid for one year, and your part-time employer must pay an AED 600 fee.

This cost consists of two main fees, which are the application fee (AED 100) and the approval fee (AED 500). Another important detail that must be considered is the consequences of working for another company without a work permit. In this case, the hiring company or organization must face a fine of AED 50,000.

In order to apply for this permit, you will need these documents:

  • A passport copy.
  • A colored photograph of the applicant.
  • NOC letter from sponsor (if applicable).
  • A copy of the business’s trade licenses.
  • Copy of the residency visa.
  • A copy of the new work contract.
  • Relevant academic qualifications.
  • A letter of approval from the pertinent authorities.

How can Connectfz help you obtain more information about the NOC in the UAE?

As you can see, the NOC in UAE is necessary in order to work in the country or abroad. Besides, it is also useful when applying for a specific visa or purchasing a property in the UAE. Therefore, you should request consultancy services in case you need help to obtain your NOC letter.

However, if you have already built your business, you can make it more efficient with support services. For example, requesting recruitment services is the best option to find and hire the employees you need. title: Opening a Non-Resident Bank Account in the UAE for your Business
content:
Opening a non resident bank account UAE is a strategic move. Particularly true for businesses looking to tap into the vibrant market. Everyone is aware of the UAE’s robust banking infrastructure and favorable economic conditions. This makes it an attractive destination for international entrepreneurs.

Therefore, setting up a non-resident account enables businesses to manage their finances efficiently. They can conduct transactions while accessing local banking services. Even without the need for UAE residency. Knowing the in-depth requirements and processes knowledge involved is crucial. It is essential for a seamless banking experience! A supportive move for your business objectives in this thriving environment.

Understanding Non-Resident Bank Accounts in the UAE

Individuals have the opportunity to manage their finances without needing residency status. It is possible if they have a non resident bank account UAE. These accounts are popular among expatriates and international investors. This is due to the UAE’s favorable banking regulations and tax benefits.

Further, non-residents can access various banking services, including:

·       Online banking

·       International wire transfers, and

·       Multi-currency accounts.

Note that, requirements may vary between banks. It often necessitates specific documentation. The documents like proof of identity and source of funds. In short, non-resident accounts provide a convenient way to conduct financial transactions in a stable economic environment.

What is a Non-Resident Bank Account?

In the UAE, a non-resident bank account is designed for businesses that do not reside in the country. Even though they are not currently residing but wish to conduct financial transactions within its banking system. The accounts efficiently manage funds for them. The non-residents can engage in no time with their local business activities and investments. All can be possible by having a non-resident bank account in the UAE.

Benefits of Having a Non-Resident Bank Account in the UAE

Having a non-resident bank account provides several advantages, including:

·       It offers easy access to UAE’s financial services

·       Non-resident bank account has the ability to transact in local currency.

·       It allows businesses to benefit from the UAE’s tax-friendly environment and robust economic stability

·       It enables organizations to enhance their operational capabilities.

Eligibility Criteria for Non-Resident Bank Accounts

To open a non-resident bank account, applicants need to provide:

·       Valid identification

·       Proof of business ownership, and

·       Documentation regarding the source of funds

Sometimes, banks may also require additional information. It is primarily based on their internal policies and the applicant’s country of origin.

Types of Non-Resident Bank Accounts Available

Non-residents can choose from various account types in the UAE. These may include personal accounts, corporate accounts, and savings accounts. Each account type offers different features and services. Select wisely by realizing your specific needs. They cater accordingly to the business’s requirements looking to manage finances effectively.

Currency Options for Non-Resident Accounts

The Dubai bank account for non residents offers multiple currency options. It allows account holders to transact in AED. They can also use it in other major currencies like USD, EUR, and GBP. This flexibility enables businesses to conduct international transactions seamlessly. Ultimately, they can manage currency risk more effectively.

Documents Required to Open a Non-Resident Bank Account

Are you all up to open your non-resident bank account in the UAE? Give yourself a pause and think about the necessary documents that you may need. Here, we give you a brief list. Gather it first and then move forward!

Essential Documents for Account Opening

To open a non resident bank account UAE, you need to provide:

·       A valid passport

·       Proof of business ownership, and

·       A completed application form

However, some banks may also require a reference letter from your current bank to ensure credibility.

Additional Documents for Specific Account Types

Additional documents may be required. It depends on the account type you wish to open. Corporate accounts may need articles of incorporation or partnership agreements. On the other hand, savings accounts might require proof of savings goals.

Proof of Income and Financial Status

Many banks require proof of income to assess your financial standing and ability to maintain the account. This can include recent bank statements, tax returns, or salary slips that demonstrate your income source and stability.

Address Verification

Address verification is necessary for compliance with anti-money laundering regulations. Show utility bills, lease agreements, or official correspondence. All information must display your name and current residential address.

Passport and Visa Requirements

A valid passport is essential for a company bank account opening in UAE. It verifies your identity. A visa may be required. However, it depends on the bank. This ensures compliance with local regulations. Particularly for corporate accounts linked to your business activities in the UAE.

How to Open a Non-Resident Bank Account in the UAE

Opening your non resident bank account UAE is a simple process. A step-by-step procedure has been shared. It helps you open your non-resident bank account in the UAE. So, let’s explore this in detail.

Step-by-Step Guide to Account Opening

In the UAE, opening a non-resident bank account involves a series of steps. Firstly, gather the required documents. Then schedule an appointment with your chosen bank. There you need to submit your application and documentation for review.

Choosing the Right Bank

For meeting your specific needs, the right bank selection is a game-changer. Research various banks to compare their fees, services, and account types. Make sure to choose one that aligns with your business goals and offers convenient banking options.

Account Activation and Access

The bank will provide you with account details once your application is approved. They let you know about the access methods. Typically, you’ll receive online banking credentials. This allows you to manage your account. You can conduct transactions and monitor activity from anywhere in the world.

Security Measures for Your Account

Banks implement various security measures to safeguard your non-resident bank account. This includes:

·       Two-factor authentication and

·       Encryption protocols

However, it is essential to follow best practices. You can use strong passwords and regularly monitor account activity. This in turn helps to protect your financial information.

Challenges and Considerations for Non-Resident Account Holders

With every ease, there must be some challenges involved to address. This is true when we talk about having and managing a non-resident account. Listing down a few challenges and considerations that should be kept in mind as a non-resident account holder.

Tax Implications for Non-Resident Accounts

Tax implications are a must to know for non-resident account holders. The taxes can be applied in both their home country and the UAE. It highly depends on the jurisdiction. However, the interest earned on the account may be subject to taxation. Here comes a need to consult a tax advisor for compliance.

Currency Exchange and Transfer Fees

For non-residents, currency exchange and transfer fees can impact the overall banking cost. So, it’s important to understand the fees of converting currencies and making international transfers. As they can vary widely between banks.

Account Maintenance and Closure

Non-resident accounts come with maintenance fees. These charges can add up over time. Furthermore, the process for account closure is crucial to understand. As it may involve specific requirements and potential fees. This could affect your financial planning.

Alternative Banking Options for Non-Residents

Non-residents may consider alternative banking options in addition to traditional banks. They can use online banks or fintech solutions. These options can provide competitive fees and innovative services. It makes it easier to manage finances from abroad efficiently.

Online Banking and Mobile Apps

Most banks in the UAE offer online banking and mobile app services. This feasibility allows non-residents to manage their accounts conveniently. Typically, these digital platforms provide features such as:

·       Fund transfers

·       Transaction monitoring, and

·       Account management

This in turn enhances accessibility to effortlessly use and manage your bank account at just your fingertips!

Fraud Prevention and Security

Non-resident account holders should prioritize security to protect against fraud. Banks implement various measures, such as transaction alerts and secure login protocols, but individuals must also practice vigilance, including monitoring account activity and using secure connections.

Tips for Managing Your Non-Resident Bank Account

Before tapping into opening your non-resident bank account, must know how to manage it effectively. Several tips are penned down that help you manage your non-resident bank account in the UAE.

Maximizing Your Account Benefits

Familiarize yourself with all available features and services. This helps you to get the most out of your non-resident bank account. These may involve:

·       Online banking tools

·       Loyalty programs, and Regularly reviewing account statements and fee structures understanding can also help you avoid unnecessary charges. So, that you can optimize your financial strategy accordingly.

Customer Support and Assistance

It is advisable to establish a good relationship with your bank’s customer support. As it can significantly enhance your banking experience. Don’t hesitate to reach them for assistance with account management. They are good at resolving your issues in the blink of an eye. They also assist you in understanding banking products. Many banks offer dedicated support for non-resident clients, ensuring you receive timely and relevant help whenever needed.

Conclusion

In a nutshell, opening a non resident bank account UAE makes for a strategic move and greatly lifts the operations of your business out there. Taking up the understanding of requirements, benefits, and the processes involved will thus facilitate effective management of one’s finances as one seeks to take advantage of such a robust banking infrastructure. With the right account, you receive all kinds of services designed to enable you to make transactions, spur growth, and keep your money safe. As you walk through this process, using customer support to maximize the features available in your accounts will further ensure that your banking experience and business are working toward predetermined goals, paving the way to success in this dynamic market.

title: What should you know about overtime calculation in UAE?
content:
Overtime calculation in UAE is a common practice in companies to pay employees for this working time. However, there are laws to make these calculations and thus guarantee the rights of workers in the Emirates. In the same way, with this law, the aim is to pay the employee fairly for the hours of work addition to the regular ones.

In this article, you will see the important aspects of workers who work overtime and the laws that protect them. Moreover, you will learn how to do the calculations to properly complete payments on your company in UAE.

Overtime calculation in UAE as Per Labor Law

Overtime is the time the employee works outside of normal working hours. Likewise, they receive a payment for these overtime hours that the employer will have to make through the overtime calculation in UAE. However, overtime work does not necessarily mean that the employee will receive payment.

Thus, to understand the difference, you can include the overtime that a worker may have worked voluntarily. However, you may not qualify for overtime pay in certain particular cases. Therefore, under current labor laws, employees will have their rights protected as follows:

  • Article 17-1 of Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 of the New Employment Law on the Regulation of Labor Relations in the private sector. In this decree, the law establishes that the maximum working day is 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week.
  • Article 17-2. This establishes that the cabinet may increase daily working hours according to prior agreement with the Ministry or any interested entity. However, this is only for certain types of workers or economic sectors. Likewise, concerning rest periods and schedules, it will be prohibited for some categories of employees.

Similarly, overtime will not apply to the following jobs:

  • Administrative Supervision Functions
  • Senior positions
  • Warship crews and Navy employees

How is Overtime Calculated in Payroll Under UAE Law?

For employers, there are some obligations imposed by law that they must comply with towards their employees. However, it will depend on the contract or job position, labor covetousness, housing, and sick leave, among others. Below are some provisions to take into account when doing the UAE overtime calculation online:

  • An employee is entitled to receive overtime compensation for any work performed after normal working hours. However, this will be possible as long as you are not in a managerial position.
  • The time spent traveling by an employee to his or her residence or vice versa is not counted as a working day. Nevertheless, there are exceptions as established by the so-called Executive Regulations herein. Furthermore, it will not apply to all job profiles so they can agree with employers whether it will be convenient or not.
  • Employees will not be able to work for two consecutive days of rest unless they are day laborers.
  • If the employee is full-time, the employer cannot force the worker to work overtime beyond the hours established by the contract. However, if the employee wishes to do so, he or she may agree with his or her employer.
  • When the employee wants to do a job remotely, within or outside the Emirates with the permission of the employer. At this point, you will be able to specify the number of hours of work you will do.

What to Do in Case of Disagreements?

The labor law states that the employee may receive between 25% and 50% of the usual salary for the hours of additional work. However, some exceptions and factors vary, such as the worker’s position, the day and time, and the nature of the work. Likewise, a worker will not be able to claim an overtime calculation in UAE MOHRE if he or she is not in the categories authorized by him.

Also, if there is any disagreement with some established regulations and the employer’s obligations, they may contact MOHRE. Therefore, it will be the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization that will decide if the worker is a candidate to receive payment for their overtime hours worked.

Also, there is something you can do if your employer does not pay the overtime according to the Labor Law and its executive regulations. In this case, you can explain your problem to the MOHRE advice center at the number 04 665 9999.

Rules Related to the Working Hours in the UAE

To carry out a correct overtime calculation in UAE, it is also necessary to know the rules that regulate working hours. Next, we will show you what these key rules are that you must know to defend your rights:

  • Federal Decree-Law No. 33 in Article 17, about the regulations of labor laws, establishes working hours at 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week.
  • The working day may be increased or decreased depending on the economic sector or the categories of the worker.
  • The time used by the employee for travel is not considered part of the work schedule unless it falls within certain categories.
  • If the employee works for several employers at the same time, they may not require the employee to work overtime outside of that applied in the contract. Unless the employee is the one who decides and leaves it in writing.
  • If the employee requests to work remotely either in another region of the Emirates or anywhere else in the world. In this case, it is the employer who will have a particular schedule.
  • An employee will have the right to have several breaks if he has worked for 5 continuous hours. Furthermore, breaks cannot be less than 1 hour and will not be included in the UAE overtime calculation.

Key Rules Related to Working Overtime in the UAE

There are certain rules for calculating overtime in UAE MOHRE as you can see below:

  • Employers can impose overtime on their employees, as long as it does not exceed 2 hours a day.
  • When a worker must work longer than usual hours, he or she will have the right to receive additional payment. Also, the compensation will be equal to a few days of normal work plus 25% extra and could increase if they work between 10 pm and 4 am. Furthermore, the exception to this rule applies to workers whose workday is in shifts.
  • If the employee works on his or her day off, it will apply as overtime and the employer must provide a substitute day off or compensation. Likewise, said compensation will be 50% additional to the corresponding salary per day.
  • When the employee exceeds 5 overtime hours, the employer will allow him or her to rest for no less than 1 hour.
  • The time to travel to the workplace of the employees or the hours spent eating will not apply as overtime. Nor any hour of rest granted between overtime hours of work.

title: Key Points About Part-Time Work Permits in the UAE
content:
Part time work permit UAE is not something that many employers can offer their employees. Having flexibility as a worker can help you earn more income and for this reason part time work is a great option. If you are working less than 8 hours, part time work in UAE can be considered.

In this article we are going to explain in depth the key points about part time work permit UAE, what are the eligible aspects for such permit, what are the benefits, the step by step to apply for it, the cost and the renewal of this permit.

Key Eligibility Criteria for Part-Time Work Permits in UAE

Part time work UAE is available to any UAE resident, whether currently employed or not. You are also eligible for the temporary work permit if you are a GCC national or expatriate employee living in the UAE on a work visa.

Please note that the part time work permit UAE contract system is limited to skilled workers only. This means that a university degree or higher is usually require. You are also eligible if you have completed a two or three year diploma in a technical or scientific field.

Also, people living in the UAE on a family visa can accept a second job. You will need to receive a part time work permit UAE with an NOC from the sponsor. These work permits are available for men and women aged 18 and 65.

Please note that persons on visitor or tourist visas cannot apply for a part time work permit UAE. Only expatriates or residents may apply:

  • Age limit: 18 years old. Anyone below the age limit cannot obtain a part-time UAE work permit.
  • It is mandatory to have a valid UAE residence visa. You have to be a resident of the UAE to obtain a part-time work permit.
  • The applicant must have a permanent job and work permit.
  • Expatriates are also eligible for a part-time work permit if they are in the UAE on a family visa.
  • UAE tourist visa holders are not eligible to engage in any part-time work in the UAE.
  • If the person is over 65 years of age, he or she cannot apply for a part-time work permit.

Understanding the Cost of Part-Time Work Permits

Among the requirements of the part time work permit UAE is its cost. The first thing you should know is that the cost of issuing or renewing the permit varies depending on the classification of the company.

This classification reflects the company’s level of compliance with labor laws. In addition, the Wage Protection System, relevant resolutions and directives of the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, laws on workers’ rights and other regulations.

With this in mind, the part-time work permit UAE cost permit can be obtained. This can range from AED 250 to AED 3450. Also, the Department of Health’s processing time for a temporary work permit application depends on a variety of factors.

Step-by-Step Application Process for Part-Time Work Permits in UAE

The process of obtaining a part time work permit UAE or temporary work visa is straightforward. You have to obtain permission from MoHRE, and the process is usually the responsibility of the employer. You can apply for a visa through the ministry’s website or by visiting the office in person.

Please note that the permit is usually valid for six months. The part-time visa permit costs AED 600 in total, and includes the application fee (AED 100) and the approval fee (AED 500). The prospective employer will be responsible for the payment of the fees.

  • Log in with your username and password or use UAE Pass (online/smart channels only).
  • Send your request through one of our service channels.
  • The application will be forwarded electronically to the Ministry for verification of compliance with the requirements and documents.
  • Gaps will be communicated to the facility for completion.
  • Upon completion of all requirements and documents, the issuance of a part-time work permit shall be approved
  • Payment of federal fees upon approval.

Essential Requirements for Obtaining a Part-Time Work Permit in UAE

The documents for the part-time work permit UAE requirements are as follows:

  • A copy of the business licenses of both companies (the current/main company and the applicant/secondary company).
  • One color photograph with white background of the worker
  • Copy of the employee’s passport
  • If an academic qualification (post-secondary diploma, university degree or equivalent) is required, a copy of the qualification must be attached and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
  • A letter of approval issued by the competent authority shall be attached if required (doctor, pharmacist, nurse and teacher)
  • Copy of the contract
  • Certificate of no objection from the former sponsor/principal sponsor
  • A copy of the worker’s visa including the name of the sponsor or establishment which must be valid for more than 6 months.

Exploring the Benefits of Part-Time Work Permits in UAE

The implementation of Ministerial Decision No. 31 news for both employees and business owners in the United Arab Emirates. Before there were legal provisions, part time work permit UAE was a very difficult thing to offer.

However, once this type of work arrangement was valid, it started to give several benefits to employees and employers in the UAE. Some of the most notable part time work permit UAE benefits ones are as follows:

  • Employers who do not have enough budget for full-time workers can hire part-time employees.
  • It allows employers to hire the workers they need and offer them the best deal.
  • Employees who just want to work fewer hours can do so and earn the income they want.
  • Allows employees who want to have more than one role to do so. It is especially good for students
  • Part-time employee roles can be created by employers for specific projects.
  • Such benefits apply in many fields, even if we talk about part-time jobs for women in Dubai, because they provide opportunities for many people in the UAE.

Renewing and Extending Your Part-Time Work Permit in the UAE

Extending your temporary work permit means applying for a new work permit from the same employer. Of course, this will be after the previous permit expires. All temporary work permits have duration of six months. Moreover, you can only renew it once and you will be granted the same period.

Besides, extending this work permit means applying for an additional work permit from another employer. However, this does not cancel the previous permit. Any UAE temporary work permit can be extended for an additional period of up to six months. To do so, the worker must have the consent of the main employer.

To renew a part time work permit UAE, simply follow the steps below:

  • The worker must submit the temporary work permit renewal application form.
  • Attach the necessary documents. For example, the job offer, photocopy of passport and visa, medical certificate, and others. The documents are generally the same as the permit application form.
  • Pay the corresponding fees, which will vary depending on the classification of the company.
  • Send your renewal application to the Ministry of Manpower and Human Resources (MOHR). Another option is to go to the competent authority of the free zone where you work.

If you want to apply for the extension of your part time work permit UAE, you can start with the following steps:

  • The employer must give his consent to the worker through a letter containing his stamp and signature.
  • The new employer must apply for additional work permits for the employee.
  • MoHRE will verify the eligibility of the new employer and the employee. the extension will be issued if the requirements are fulfilled. It is important to note that this can only be done once and has the same duration, i.e. 6 months.

Navigating the Cancellation Process for Part-Time Work Permits in the UAE

To part time work permit UAE cancellation, follow these steps:

  • Employer Application: Your employer must submit the application through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MoHRE). You will submit the required documents electronically.
  • Processing by MoHRE: MoHRE temporarily processes the application and forwards the information to the General Directorate of Residency and Aliens (GDRFA).
  • Cancellation by the GDRFA: The GDRFA cancels your UAE Residence Visa and informs MoHRE. Subsequently, the MoHRE permanently cancels your work permit in the UAE.

Remember that compliance with legal procedures is essential when canceling work permits. If you have any specific questions or need further assistance, please contact the relevant authorities for accurate guidance.

Make the most of your chance to obtain this part time work permit UAE in one of the most prosperous economies in the Middle East. Our team of experts is ready to answer your questions and provide you with customized solutions.

With our guidance, you can obtain a cheap business trade license for Dubai, which corresponds to your budget and start working immediately. We will assess your needs and help you decide what type of license you need based on the nature of your business.
