title: How to Start a Business in Abu Dhabi (2026 Guide)
content:
Want to start a business in Abu Dhabi but feeling lost on where to begin? You’re not the only one. Every year, many people move to Abu Dhabi with a dream to launch their own business. The city is full of opportunities. It has a fast-growing economy, zero income tax, and allows full foreign ownership in many areas.

But starting a business here needs proper planning. If you miss a step, it could delay your launch or cost you more money. That’s why we’ve created this simple 2026 guide. It covers all the basics and walks you through how to start a business in Abu Dhabi the right way.

Why Abu Dhabi is the Right Place for Your Business

Abu Dhabi is quickly becoming one of the top business destinations in the world. With its advanced infrastructure, supportive government policies, and attractive tax environment, the city continues to welcome investors and entrepreneurs from all over. The UAE’s push toward diversification and innovation also means there are many open doors across various sectors.

In 2026, business registration processes are more streamlined than ever. Government portals such as TAMM and the Abu Dhabi Business Center now offer fully integrated digital services, allowing entrepreneurs to complete licensing, approvals, and renewals online. Compared to previous years, approvals are faster, documentation is clearer, and most steps can be completed without visiting government offices.

Benefits of Starting a Business in Abu Dhabi

Abu Dhabi offers more than just a location—it gives you a strong platform to grow. From money-saving policies to easy access to global markets, starting a business here comes with many real advantages.

Full Foreign Ownership

Many business sectors in Abu Dhabi now allow 100% foreign ownership. You can start and control your business without needing a local partner.

No Personal Income Tax

There is no personal income tax in Abu Dhabi. This means you keep more of your earnings and can reinvest in your business.

Access to Global Markets

Abu Dhabi is well connected to Asia, Europe, and Africa. This makes it easy to trade, export, and expand internationally.

Government Support Programs

New businesses can apply for grants, funding, and free training. Support is also available through business incubators and startup centers.

Strategic Location

The capital city is in a perfect spot for import and export. You can ship goods quickly and connect with partners in nearby countries.

Modern Infrastructure

Abu Dhabi has excellent roads, airports, ports, and internet systems. This helps your business run smoothly and stay efficient.

Simple Online Setup Process

Thanks to portals like TAMM, you can now complete most steps online. It saves time and reduces paperwork.

Diverse Business Opportunities

Many sectors are growing fast. Whether it’s tech, health, tourism, or manufacturing, there’s room for new ideas and companies.

One major advantage is that many sectors now allow full foreign ownership, even on the mainland. This means you don’t need a local partner to start your own company. You also benefit from zero personal income tax. However, businesses are now subject to the UAE’s federal corporate tax framework, with a standard 9% rate applied to taxable profits above the required threshold. Certain free zone entities and qualifying small businesses may still benefit from exemptions or reliefs, depending on their structure and activity. These policies keep Abu Dhabi competitive while aligning with global tax standards. These financial benefits significantly reduce your overall business costs.

The government offers various support schemes to new businesses. These include funding opportunities, grants, and dedicated assistance through business incubators and accelerators. Moreover, Abu Dhabi’s location makes it an excellent hub for companies looking to access markets in Asia, Africa, and Europe.

Popular Industries to Consider

Abu Dhabi is full of growing sectors that welcome new businesses. If you’re planning to start a business in Abu Dhabi, it helps to choose an industry with long-term demand and government support.

Technology and IT

Abu Dhabi supports tech startups through innovation hubs and funding. Software, fintech, and cybersecurity firms are growing fast.

Manufacturing

This sector is expanding under national industrial strategies. Businesses making goods like food, medicine, and materials can apply for an industrial license.

Tourism and Hospitality

With more global events and visitors, this industry offers strong opportunities. Travel agencies, hotels, and tour services are in demand.

Healthcare and Wellness

The government is investing in better medical care. Clinics, wellness centers, and medical supply companies can grow in this space.

Education and Training

More people are looking for skills and education. Online courses, training centers, and tutoring services are profitable sectors.

E-commerce and Retail

People prefer shopping online. Setting up an online store or delivery service is easier than ever.

Renewable Energy

Abu Dhabi is focusing on clean energy. Solar power and eco-friendly technology startups have long-term support here.

Step-by-Step Guide to Start a Business in Abu Dhabi

Let’s walk through each step to help you understand the process of launching your company in Abu Dhabi.

Step 1: Choose Your Business Activity

The first step is selecting a business activity that matches what you plan to offer. This could range from opening a restaurant to setting up an e-commerce platform or offering professional services. Every business activity falls under specific classifications and is linked to a certain type of license.

For instance, if you plan to run a manufacturing facility, you’ll need an industrial license. But if your focus is consulting or IT services, a professional license is more suitable. Carefully selecting the activity ensures you don’t face issues when applying for your license or expanding your business.

Step 2: Select the Legal Structure

Once your activity is clear, the next step is to pick your company’s legal form. You can choose a sole proprietorship if you’re starting alone or go for a Limited Liability Company (LLC) if you’re working with partners. An LLC is the most common structure and offers flexibility and limited personal liability.

Foreign companies can also open a branch office in Abu Dhabi to expand their operations. Your legal structure will affect how you manage ownership, liability, and tax obligations, so it’s important to choose the right one from the start.

Step 3: Reserve a Trade Name

After choosing your activity and structure, it’s time to reserve your company’s trade name. The name should reflect your business type and must be unique in the UAE. Avoid names with religious or political terms.

The Abu Dhabi Business Center allows you to check name availability and reserve it online. This step helps build your brand and makes it easier for customers to remember you.

Step 4: Apply for the Business License

Getting your license is one of the most important steps in setting up. The license type depends on your business activity. If you’re trading products, go for a commercial license. If you’re providing services, a professional license is suitable. For production or factory-related work, you’ll need an industrial license.

To start a business in abu dhabi, you’ll need to fill out an application form and submit it through the TAMM portal. Make sure all your information matches your trade name and activity.

Step 5: Get Approvals and Submit Documents

Depending on your chosen activity, you may need special approvals from certain authorities. For example, a food business might need health clearances, while an industrial business may require environmental permits.

Common documents include passport copies of owners, the initial approval letter from the Department of Economic Development (DED), your trade name certificate, and your lease agreement. Some businesses may also need a business plan or proof of experience.

All documents can be submitted online, making the process faster and smoother than in previous years.

Step 6: Rent Office Space

Most businesses need a registered address in Abu Dhabi. This could be a physical office or a co-working space, depending on your business type. If you’re applying for an industrial trade license, you must have a warehouse, factory, or appropriate industrial property.

Free zones often offer shared office spaces or virtual offices, which are ideal for startups and tech companies. Mainland businesses, however, usually require a physical address.

Step 7: Register with Relevant Authorities

Once your license is approved, you need to register with other departments to become fully operational. These include the Ministry of Labor for hiring staff and the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship for visas.

Joining the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce is also essential. It connects you with other businesses and helps you access local opportunities and events.

Free Zone vs Mainland: What’s Best for You?

Choosing between free zone and mainland depends on your business goals. Free zones offer 100% foreign ownership, simplified setup, and full repatriation of profits. They are perfect for businesses focused on exports or tech services.

Mainland setups allow you to trade directly with the UAE market and take on government contracts. However, in some cases, you may need a local sponsor. That said, many sectors now allow full foreign ownership on the mainland too.

Use the table below to compare your options:

Feature Free Zone Mainland
Ownership 100% foreign Local partner needed for some sectors
Tax Benefits Corporate tax exemption Subject to corporate tax laws
Office Space Optional Often required
Market Reach Global Full UAE market access

 

Understanding the Industrial Trade License

The industrial trade license is needed for businesses that produce, manufacture, or process goods. This includes food packaging, textiles, equipment manufacturing, and more.

In Abu Dhabi, applying for this license requires a detailed business plan, a physical facility, and approvals from the Department of Economic Development and other government bodies. You may also need clearance from environmental and safety departments, depending on your activity.

This license supports Abu Dhabi’s economic diversification goals. The government is actively encouraging industrial businesses through incentives such as land grants, utility discounts, and funding opportunities.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even with a smooth process in place, many business owners make small mistakes that lead to big delays. Knowing what to avoid can help you save time and money.

Picking the Wrong License Type

Many entrepreneurs choose a license that doesn’t match their business activity. For example, someone planning to manufacture goods might apply for a professional license instead of an industrial license. This causes delays, fines, and in some cases, suspension of business operations.

Skipping Professional Consultation

A lot of business owners think they can do everything on their own. While online portals make it easier, missing one document or selecting the wrong legal form can create long-term problems. Getting advice from a business consultant can save time and prevent expensive errors.

Using a Trade Name That Gets Rejected

Another common issue is choosing a business name that violates UAE naming rules. Names with religious, political, or offensive terms are automatically denied. This slows down the process and might require you to restart the name approval step.

Renting an Inappropriate Office Space

Many first-time business owners rent a space before finalizing their license. If the space doesn’t meet the government’s criteria—especially for those applying for an industrial trade license—your application may be rejected. Always check property requirements based on your license type first.

Ignoring Local Regulations

Some entrepreneurs assume that rules are the same across the UAE. But Abu Dhabi has specific requirements different from Dubai or Sharjah. Not reviewing the local rules can lead to rejections or legal trouble later.

Underestimating Setup Costs

Some people budget only for license fees but forget about other expenses like visas, insurance, office rent, or municipality approvals. This can stretch your budget and delay your launch. Always calculate the full cost before you begin. new entrepreneurs make mistakes that delay their business launch. One of the most common issues is choosing the wrong license. If your license doesn’t match your business activity, you may face penalties or forced closure.

How Much Does It Cost to Start a Business in Abu Dhabi?

Costs vary depending on your license type, business activity, and location. On average, a small service business can cost between AED 15,000 and AED 25,000 to set up. If you’re applying for an industrial trade license, the cost can go up to AED 50,000 or more.

These fees include trade name registration, license issuance, office rent, and other government charges. Free zones may offer packages that bundle multiple services together at a lower rate.

Be sure to plan for hidden costs like employee visas, insurance, and renewal fees. A well-managed budget can help you avoid unexpected surprises.

Build with Confidence: Partner with Connect Fz

Starting a business in Abu Dhabi can feel overwhelming. But the right partner can make your journey smooth and stress-free.

Your Shortcut to Starting a Business in Abu Dhabi

Starting a business in Abu Dhabi becomes faster and easier with the right support. Connect Fz helps you with everything—licenses, approvals, office space, and legal paperwork.

Whether you’re going for a simple commercial setup or a full industrial trade license, Connect Fz makes it hassle-free. Their experts guide you from the first step to the final approval, giving you peace of mind and more time to focus on growing your business.

Want to start a business in Abu Dhabi without delays? Let Connect Fz handle the hard part so you can focus on success.

Government portals such as TAMM and the Abu Dhabi Business Center now offer fully integrated digital services, allowing entrepreneurs to complete licensing, approvals, and renewals online. Compared to previous years, approvals are faster, documentation is clearer, and most steps can be completed without visiting government offices.

Benefits of Starting a Business in Abu Dhabi

Abu Dhabi offers more than just a location—it gives you a strong platform to grow. From money-saving policies to easy access to global markets, starting a business here comes with many real advantages.

Full Foreign Ownership

Many business sectors in Abu Dhabi now allow 100% foreign ownership. You can start and control your business without needing a local partner.

No Personal Income Tax

There is no personal income tax in Abu Dhabi. This means you keep more of your earnings and can reinvest in your business.

Access to Global Markets

Abu Dhabi is well connected to Asia, Europe, and Africa. This makes it easy to trade, export, and expand internationally.

Government Support Programs

New businesses can apply for grants, funding, and free training. Support is also available through business incubators and startup centers.

Strategic Location

The capital city is in a perfect spot for import and export. You can ship goods quickly and connect with partners in nearby countries.

Modern Infrastructure

Abu Dhabi has excellent roads, airports, ports, and internet systems. This helps your business run smoothly and stay efficient.

Simple Online Setup Process

Thanks to portals like TAMM, you can now complete most steps online. It saves time and reduces paperwork.

Diverse Business Opportunities

Many sectors are growing fast. Whether it’s tech, health, tourism, or manufacturing, there’s room for new ideas and companies.

One major advantage is that many sectors now allow full foreign ownership, even on the mainland. This means you don’t need a local partner to start your own company. You also benefit from zero personal income tax. However, businesses are now subject to the UAE’s federal corporate tax framework, with a standard 9% rate applied to taxable profits above the required threshold. Certain free zone entities and qualifying small businesses may still benefit from exemptions or reliefs, depending on their structure and activity. These policies keep Abu Dhabi competitive while aligning with global tax standards. These financial benefits significantly reduce your overall business costs.

The government offers various support schemes to new businesses. These include funding opportunities, grants, and dedicated assistance through business incubators and accelerators. Moreover, Abu Dhabi’s location makes it an excellent hub for companies looking to access markets in Asia, Africa, and Europe.

Popular Industries to Consider

Abu Dhabi is full of growing sectors that welcome new businesses. If you’re planning to start a business in Abu Dhabi, it helps to choose an industry with long-term demand and government support.

Technology and IT

Abu Dhabi supports tech startups through innovation hubs and funding. Software, fintech, and cybersecurity firms are growing fast.

Manufacturing

This sector is expanding under national industrial strategies. Businesses making goods like food, medicine, and materials can apply for an industrial license.

Tourism and Hospitality

With more global events and visitors, this industry offers strong opportunities. Travel agencies, hotels, and tour services are in demand.

Healthcare and Wellness

The government is investing in better medical care. Clinics, wellness centers, and medical supply companies can grow in this space.

Education and Training

More people are looking for skills and education. Online courses, training centers, and tutoring services are profitable sectors.

E-commerce and Retail

People prefer shopping online. Setting up an online store or delivery service is easier than ever.

Renewable Energy

Abu Dhabi is focusing on clean energy. Solar power and eco-friendly technology startups have long-term support here.

Step-by-Step Guide to Start a Business in Abu Dhabi

Let’s walk through each step to help you understand the process of launching your company in Abu Dhabi.

Step 1: Choose Your Business Activity

The first step is selecting a business activity that matches what you plan to offer. This could range from opening a restaurant to setting up an e-commerce platform or offering professional services. Every business activity falls under specific classifications and is linked to a certain type of license.

For instance, if you plan to run a manufacturing facility, you’ll need an industrial license. But if your focus is consulting or IT services, a professional license is more suitable. Carefully selecting the activity ensures you don’t face issues when applying for your license or expanding your business.

Step 2: Select the Legal Structure

Once your activity is clear, the next step is to pick your company’s legal form. You can choose a sole proprietorship if you’re starting alone or go for a Limited Liability Company (LLC) if you’re working with partners. An LLC is the most common structure and offers flexibility and limited personal liability.

Foreign companies can also open a branch office in Abu Dhabi to expand their operations. Your legal structure will affect how you manage ownership, liability, and tax obligations, so it’s important to choose the right one from the start.

Step 3: Reserve a Trade Name

After choosing your activity and structure, it’s time to reserve your company’s trade name. The name should reflect your business type and must be unique in the UAE. Avoid names with religious or political terms.

The Abu Dhabi Business Center allows you to check name availability and reserve it online. This step helps build your brand and makes it easier for customers to remember you.

Step 4: Apply for the Business License

Getting your license is one of the most important steps in setting up. The license type depends on your business activity. If you’re trading products, go for a commercial license. If you’re providing services, a professional license is suitable. For production or factory-related work, you’ll need an industrial license.

To start a business in abu dhabi, you’ll need to fill out an application form and submit it through the TAMM portal. Make sure all your information matches your trade name and activity.

Step 5: Get Approvals and Submit Documents

Depending on your chosen activity, you may need special approvals from certain authorities. For example, a food business might need health clearances, while an industrial business may require environmental permits.

Common documents include passport copies of owners, the initial approval letter from the Department of Economic Development (DED), your trade name certificate, and your lease agreement. Some businesses may also need a business plan or proof of experience.

All documents can be submitted online, making the process faster and smoother than in previous years.

Step 6: Rent Office Space

Most businesses need a registered address in Abu Dhabi. This could be a physical office or a co-working space, depending on your business type. If you’re applying for an industrial trade license, you must have a warehouse, factory, or appropriate industrial property.

Free zones often offer shared office spaces or virtual offices, which are ideal for startups and tech companies. Mainland businesses, however, usually require a physical address.

Step 7: Register with Relevant Authorities

Once your license is approved, you need to register with other departments to become fully operational. These include the Ministry of Labor for hiring staff and the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship for visas.

Joining the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce is also essential. It connects you with other businesses and helps you access local opportunities and events.

Free Zone vs Mainland: What’s Best for You?

Choosing between free zone and mainland depends on your business goals. Free zones offer 100% foreign ownership, simplified setup, and full repatriation of profits. They are perfect for businesses focused on exports or tech services.

Mainland setups allow you to trade directly with the UAE market and take on government contracts. However, in some cases, you may need a local sponsor. That said, many sectors now allow full foreign ownership on the mainland too.

Use the table below to compare your options:

Feature Free Zone Mainland
Ownership 100% foreign Local partner needed for some sectors
Tax Benefits Corporate tax exemption Subject to corporate tax laws
Office Space Optional Often required
Market Reach Global Full UAE market access

 

Understanding the Industrial Trade License

The industrial trade license is needed for businesses that produce, manufacture, or process goods. This includes food packaging, textiles, equipment manufacturing, and more.

In Abu Dhabi, applying for this license requires a detailed business plan, a physical facility, and approvals from the Department of Economic Development and other government bodies. You may also need clearance from environmental and safety departments, depending on your activity.

This license supports Abu Dhabi’s economic diversification goals. The government is actively encouraging industrial businesses through incentives such as land grants, utility discounts, and funding opportunities.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even with a smooth process in place, many business owners make small mistakes that lead to big delays. Knowing what to avoid can help you save time and money.

Picking the Wrong License Type

Many entrepreneurs choose a license that doesn’t match their business activity. For example, someone planning to manufacture goods might apply for a professional license instead of an industrial license. This causes delays, fines, and in some cases, suspension of business operations.

Skipping Professional Consultation

A lot of business owners think they can do everything on their own. While online portals make it easier, missing one document or selecting the wrong legal form can create long-term problems. Getting advice from a business consultant can save time and prevent expensive errors.

Using a Trade Name That Gets Rejected

Another common issue is choosing a business name that violates UAE naming rules. Names with religious, political, or offensive terms are automatically denied. This slows down the process and might require you to restart the name approval step.

Renting an Inappropriate Office Space

Many first-time business owners rent a space before finalizing their license. If the space doesn’t meet the government’s criteria—especially for those applying for an industrial trade license—your application may be rejected. Always check property requirements based on your license type first.

Ignoring Local Regulations

Some entrepreneurs assume that rules are the same across the UAE. But Abu Dhabi has specific requirements different from Dubai or Sharjah. Not reviewing the local rules can lead to rejections or legal trouble later.

Underestimating Setup Costs

Some people budget only for license fees but forget about other expenses like visas, insurance, office rent, or municipality approvals. This can stretch your budget and delay your launch. Always calculate the full cost before you begin. new entrepreneurs make mistakes that delay their business launch. One of the most common issues is choosing the wrong license. If your license doesn’t match your business activity, you may face penalties or forced closure.

How Much Does It Cost to Start a Business in Abu Dhabi?

Costs vary depending on your license type, business activity, and location. On average, a small service business can cost between AED 15,000 and AED 25,000 to set up. If you’re applying for an industrial trade license, the cost can go up to AED 50,000 or more.

These fees include trade name registration, license issuance, office rent, and other government charges. Free zones may offer packages that bundle multiple services together at a lower rate.

Be sure to plan for hidden costs like employee visas, insurance, and renewal fees. A well-managed budget can help you avoid unexpected surprises.

Build with Confidence: Partner with Connect Fz

Starting a business in Abu Dhabi can feel overwhelming. But the right partner can make your journey smooth and stress-free.

Your Shortcut to Starting a Business in Abu Dhabi

Starting a business in Abu Dhabi becomes faster and easier with the right support. Connect Fz helps you with everything—licenses, approvals, office space, and legal paperwork.

Whether you’re going for a simple commercial setup or a full industrial trade license, Connect Fz makes it hassle-free. Their experts guide you from the first step to the final approval, giving you peace of mind and more time to focus on growing your business.

Want to start a business in Abu Dhabi without delays? Let Connect Fz handle the hard part so you can focus on success.

title: What is a Construction License in Dubai?
content:
Dubai and the UAE have been on the development path for several years. Likewise, the government is constantly introducing infrastructural reforms to expand the growth prospects. This causes an increase in residential and commercial constructions. Thus, obtaining a construction license in Dubai, UAE, is a great option.

In this article, we will make sure you understand everything about the process of obtaining a construction license and its types. In the same vein, you will learn why is a good idea to get a construction license. On the other hand, we will show you all the step-by-step processes and the required documents.

The construction industry in the UAE

This beautiful country has established a benchmark in every sector like architecture, modern infrastructure, tourism, and others. Similarly, the UAE has achieved many things in such a short time; mainly because of its pro-development and investor-friendly policies and government practices.

One of our main cities, Dubai, has fascinated the world since the beginning, even when it was not a famous emirate of the UAE. In the last years, the fascination reached its highest point. In addition, the city’s charm lies in its stunning open spaces, fancy buildings, top-notch infrastructure, pristine beaches, and rich culture.

Further, its GDP makes it a favoring location for obtaining a construction license in Dubai, starting a business, or seeking life quality.

In the same vein, these advantages resulted in high demand for housing or office spaces combined with long-term development initiatives such as the transformation of Expo 2020 into Expo City Dubai and the implementation of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan. As a result, Dubai is currently witnessing one of its biggest construction eras.

Investors and entrepreneurs have discovered the potential of starting a Dubai construction company. Thus, this resulted in a series of applications to the DED (Department of Economic Development); which is the government body in charge of issuing construction licenses.

Above all, you must have in mind that starting any type of business requires you to get permits, licenses, and approvals from different government entities in Dubai.

On the other hand, the diversification of the economy will play an important role in starting up a new avenue for individuals to invest in the construction sector of the UAE. In addition, this diversification resulted in the lowering of construction-related costs. For instance, the UAE has one of the most inexpensive construction costs than other high-standard cities around the globe.

What should I know about the construction licenses in Dubai?

Dubai continues to lead the GCC region in large-scale mixed-use, residential, hospitality, and infrastructure developments. Similarly, the city is an important center to the world’s highest building, the ‘Burj Khalifa’; subsequently, it increases tourism. These are two of the reasons investors a giving top priority to the construction sector in the city; travel and tourism.

And to start your business you must obtain a construction license in Dubai, UAE apart from other permits. However, these are the essential points to obtain a construction license in the UAE:

  • This type of license is commercial. In the same vein, you must apply for it at the Department of Economic Development, which is the official government entity for business setup in Dubai Mainland; or if you are establishing in a Free Zone, you must apply for your license to your free zone authority.
  • You must comply with the latest Dubai Municipality Building Regulations and construction codes before starting operations.
  • On the other hand, if you want to manage the project, as well as an engineering consultant and design; you must apply for a Professional type of license.
  • In addition, you can hire engineers and consultants who can start working after you obtain the permits. Likewise, these consultants evaluate the soil of the construction site and determine its properties.
  • After you obtain approval from the DED for the construction area; you must also obtain special approval from other government departments.
  • For instance, you must get obtain a building permit that allows you to start the activities.
  • Apply for the appropriate building permits and contractor classification approvals issued by Dubai Municipality, depending on your project scope.

What are the Types of Construction Licenses in Dubai?

There are various types of construction licenses; however, each has unique regulations and different requirements. Let’s observe:

Construction of all types of facilities and buildings

This is a commercial type of license. A company with this type of business license in Dubai is allowed to engage in construction activities of all types and for different uses. For instance:

  • General maintenance.
  • Interior decoration.
  • Sanitary plumbing.
  • Building adjusting.

However, the number of floors is set by the Dubai Municipality.

Foundation and concrete works

This is foundation construction and walls, the concrete casting of warehouse and industrial floors as well as reinforcements of cracks with concrete.

Construction of special facilities

With this type of construction license, you can build sewage disposal plants, pipelines, airport sites, electric power substations, and seaports.

Construction of metal of steel structures

This is also a commercial license. Steel contracting license in Dubai and the UAE is specialized for steel constructions. In addition, it is also specialized in the execution of all civil works activities such as installations, lay connections, floor paving, and foundation pilling. Further, installing prefabricated steel structures such as warehouses, hangars, sheds, factories, bridges, and tunnels.

In other words, construction firms engaged in these structures, are classified under class 2811; and the number of floors is set by Dubai Municipality.

Facade and finishing works

External or internal wall covering of residential, industrial, or commercial facilities with any materials.

Landscape Gardening

Organization, improvement, development of gardens and parks, arrangement of cottage grounds and villas.

Maintenance of facilities on a turnkey solution

This type of maintenance license in the city allows only for the maintenance of buildings. In addition, it excludes any extensions or equipment available inside. Further, these operations include reparations and restoration of walls, columns, floors, roofs, and others.

In the same vein, it does not matter the construction business you want to start, you must take into account the provisions of the building law created in 2013. Certainly, for official permission of a commercial license giving you the official allowance to start your business formation in the city.

Special Approvals for Starting a Dubai Construction Company

As we mentioned earlier, starting a business in the UAE requires several special permits. Regarding the construction business, there can be clearances from civil works and environmental departments. However, here is a list of some of the mandatory approvals from the government:

  • Electricity and water department: complying with these two authorities is compulsory because it provides essential services to the occupants.
  • Irrigation and Drainage Department: this permit will provide liquid waste management and other disposable areas.
  • Dubai Civil Defense Authority and Building Department: these two entities will check if the construction business is complying with the construction norms.

What is the process to obtain a construction license in Dubai, UAE?

  • Choose in what jurisdiction you want to start your construction business. That is to say, if you choose the mainland area, you will obtain the construction license in Dubai, UAE from the DED. On the other hand, if it is a Free Zone, you will receive the license from the authority in charge.
  • The UAE building department controls all aspects of construction activities in the UAE. Therefore, acquiring individual licenses requires extra approvals from the Department of Civil Protection, the Department of Road Industry, and other agencies depending on your activity area. In order to get the construction licenses, you must have technical staff and complete several processes for the accreditation of the experts.
  • Get the documents to submit them to the government authorities.
  • Pay the fees and get the license.

Business Opportunities For Construction Businesses in Dubai

In 2026, Dubai’s construction sector remains one of the most active industries in the region, supported by infrastructure expansion, sustainable housing initiatives, smart city developments, and the ongoing implementation of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.

On the other hand, the government is carrying out different projects with the focus of expanding the tourism industry. Certainly, several man-made projects like Palm Jumeirah Island, Deira Island, the maritime city, etc. have opened doors for new construction businesses in the city.

In addition, to the projects listed above, the government has unique plans to improve the transportation infrastructure. For instance, the Ongoing airport modernization and infrastructure development projects, including those connected to Dubai International Airport and Zayed International Airport, continue to create opportunities in aviation-related construction.

How can Connect Free Zone assist you to start a construction business in the UAE?

We totally understand that starting a construction business by yourself is a complicated task. For instance, the different processes, permits, and approvals are not a one-man job. That is to say, in Connect Free Zone we are here to assist you to find the best business location and PRO services in the UAE so you can start working easily.

On the other hand, we can also sponsor your business so you can start working quickly in Mainland Dubai.

We have more than 20 years of experience helping all types of business across all sectors of the UAE; that allowed us to get high-quality expertise so we can assist you all the time when you want to start your business in the country.

In Connect Free Zone we take care of the company formation process from beginning to end; allowing you to take advantage of all the benefits Dubai Mainland and Free Zone have for you. In addition, we compare facilities, locations, rules, and regulations regarding your organization’s services and objectives.

Would you like Connect Free zone to assist you to obtain a construction license in Dubai, UAE?

If you have decided you want us to start assisting you every time in obtaining the construction license; or if you have extra inquiries. You can always send us an email via contact@connectfz.com. On the other hand, you can call us at +971 4331 6688 any time you want.

Frequently Asked Questions about the construction license in Dubai

Can I set up a company a full ownership construction company in Dubai and the UAE?

In short, yes. Certainly, the amendment to company formation regulations, which come to effect on December 1st of 2020; established that you can own 100% of shares in a Dubai Mainland business. In addition, you do not require a local Emirati sponsor.

Are construction companies liable to VAT?

The UAE VAT regulations, “Services Related to Real Estate” include the supply of solutions involving the performance, coordination, and preparation of maintenance, conversion, destruction, construction, and similar work. That is to say, all construction services in the United Arab Emirates are subject to VAT.

title: How to Start a Scrap Metal Business in Dubai
content:
Dubai recycles over 4 million tonnes of metal every year, with scrap yards quietly powering one of the city’s most underrated wealth-building machines. From copper wiring to stainless steel chunks, this ‘waste’ is pure revenue, if you know how to cash in on it.

Imagine owning a business where the supply literally piles up, your raw material is everywhere, and your margins can scale with savvy logistics. The scrap metal business in Dubai is no side hustle. It is a serious goldmine wrapped in steel.

This blog post shares how you can start a scrap metal business in Dubai without burning out on red tape, license confusion, or dealing with ‘almost for sale but not really’ warehouses.

Dubai’s Scrap Metal Gold Rush: Your Blueprint to Cashing In

Dubai recycles over 70% of its construction waste, and scrap metal is the unsung hero of this green revolution. Now imagine turning discarded steel and aluminum into a thriving business. Sounds ambitious? It’s not. Meet Ravi, who moved from selling car parts to running a scrap metal business in Dubai that now nets six figures monthly. His secret? Knowing the rules, nailing logistics, and avoiding rookie mistakes. Let’s turn your scrap dream into a revenue machine without any guesswork.

Why Scrap Metal? Why Now?

  • Booming construction means more leftover metal.
  • Sustainability push = more recycling contracts.
  • Demand from Asia, Europe, and local foundries is on the rise.

But not knowing how to start a scrap business in Dubai can lead you straight into expensive licensing delays, fines, or ending up with a business that’s technically running but legally stuck.

This blog post solves that problem. So whether you’re eyeing that scrap business for sale in Dubai or want to build one from the ground up, read on.

Step 1: Pick a Business Activity That Covers Everything

In Dubai, scrap isn’t just “scrap.” There’s:

  • Ferrous metals (iron, steel)
  • Non-ferrous (copper, aluminum, brass)
  • Electronic waste
  • Industrial machinery
  • End-of-life vehicles

Make sure your trade license includes the right commercial activities. You don’t want to get flagged for trading in metal types your license doesn’t cover. Go with a free zone that allows industrial, trading, and recycling, all under one umbrella. That way, you won’t be left juggling between multiple authorities.

Step 2: Choose the Right Business Jurisdiction

Here’s where most people trip up. Not all free zones support metal trading or recycling.

Jurisdiction Best For Licensing Speed Notable Features
JAFZA Large-scale industrial scrap yards Medium Proximity to Jebel Ali Port
DMCC Precious and industrial metals Fast Best for copper, aluminum, stainless steel
Sharjah Free Zone Budget-friendly, startup-friendly Fast Easier for small traders

If you want to import/export, go with a free zone near a port. If you’re buying locally and selling to local foundries, mainland might be a better fit.

Step 3: Secure the License

To legally run a scrap metal business in Dubai, you’ll need:

  • Commercial License (trading/recycling activity)
  • Environmental Clearance (especially if storing large volumes)
  • NOC from Civil Defense (safety, fire protocols)
  • Warehouse Lease (you’ll need a physical yard or storage)

Important: You can’t apply for the environmental clearance without first securing a valid location for operations. Yes, they’ll inspect it. And yes, our team helps you with all of this without the wild goose chase across ten departments.

Step 4: Lock Down a Warehouse or Yard

This isn’t a business you can run from a co-working space. You’ll need:

  • At least 2,000–5,000 sq ft to start
  • Good access to highways or ports
  • Proper ventilation and safety protocols
  • No residential neighbors (unless you like complaints)

You can rent through the free zone or go private. Either way, the lease agreement is needed for your final license step.

Step 5: Build Supplier Networks

You’ll need steady sources of scrap. That means:

  • Contracting with construction companies for leftover steel
  • Partnering with electricians for copper and cables
  • Buying e-waste from IT firms or maintenance services
  • Attending auctions for discarded machinery

Build trust. Pay fair. And keep logistics tight. Oh, and always weigh scrap after you’ve offloaded. No one likes paying for concrete dust hidden in the pile.

Step 6: Add a Revenue Booster

You don’t just collect and stack. You:

  • Sort
  • Process (cut, compact, bundle)
  • Resell to foundries or export to India, Pakistan, or China

The better your sorting and processing, the higher your margins. A small metal shredder? Game-changer.

Step 7: Get the Paperwork Right (or Risk Fines)

To stay 100% legit, stay on top of:

  • Trade records
  • Import/export documentation
  • Weighing scale calibration logs
  • Staff safety protocols

Cut corners here and you’ll bleed out money faster than aluminum in July sun.

Start Smart: Why Setup Support Matters

Setting up a scrap metal business in Dubai isn’t rocket science. But it does involve:

  • Knowing which license to apply for
  • Avoiding hidden fines
  • Finding legit warehouse space
  • Dealing with municipality inspectors
  • Translating “what the license says” into “what you’re allowed to do”

Our team takes over the boring-but-critical backend, from business license to UAE residence visa, so you can get to the profit part.

Mistakes to Avoid (So You Don’t Lose Money)

Don’t:

  • Sign a lease before confirming it’s approved for scrap use
  • Skip the environmental clearance
  • Buy a scrap business for sale in Dubai without checking its trade license
  • Rely only on one supplier—you’ll end up empty-handed during low seasons

Do:

  • Negotiate long-term supplier contracts
  • Get a license with wide activity coverage
  • Set aside budget for safety and compliance
  • Invest in sorting machinery early

How Much Profit Are We Talking?

It’s hard to stick the label of an exact number on it. But here’s a look at what you can expect with smart sourcing:

Material Average Resale Margin Tip
Copper 30–45% Strip wires before resale
Aluminum 15–25% Clean and sort by type
Steel 10–20% Bulk sells better
E-waste Varies Sell to certified recyclers only

Margins scale with quantity, consistency, and how efficiently you process. That’s why the above margins are only an estimation.

The scrap business in Dubai isn’t glamorous… until you’re the one depositing six figures monthly. With the right license, suppliers, and grit, you’ll turn what others toss into a revenue stream that outlasts many others.
We’ve helped many entrepreneurs launch their scrap metal business in Dubai.

If you are still wondering how to start a scrap metal business in Dubai with the least fuss and the most legal clarity, we’ve got you. From choosing the best free zone to getting your hands on a UAE residence visa so you can legally operate, we help you get everything in place without the classic run-around.

Whether you’re eyeing a scrap business for sale in Dubai or want to build one from scratch, we handle the paperwork, compliance, and approvals.

Let us set up your license while you focus on stacking metal and cash.

title: Open Business in Dubai as a Foreigner: Your Step-by-Step Guide
content:
Dubai supports foreigners in starting and running businesses and encourages foreign investors to make investments in the business. The prolonged visa is one of the newest things that makes Dubai even more appealing to foreigners who intend to do business there. It permits individuals to reside in the country for an extended period and even to retire there easily.

Foreigners who intend to open a business in Dubai or another UAE Emirate can benefit from an expanding economy, political stability, tax breaks, and rapid procedures. As a foreigner starting a business in Dubai, the initial thing that you need to do is learn about the laws and procedures that you must comply with to set up your company.

You can hire business setup professionals to help you make the process easier, or you can handle it yourself. This blog post helps understand how to open a business in Dubai as a foreigner. Let’s dive into the details.

Why Open a Business as a Foreigner in Dubai Free Zones?

In the Middle East, Dubai is one of the most significant economic centers. Its location makes it easier for suppliers from the Gulf and other countries to gain access to it. Approximately 90 percent of the residents belong to other nations.

Dubai is renowned for its magnificent infrastructure. Dubai’s business climate is perfect for entrepreneurs to thrive since of its low taxes and progressive leaders who are focused on innovative technology. Starting a business in Dubai is a good idea for foreigners since it allows them to live in a place and maximize their revenue.

Dubai is open to international investment, and foreigners can develop and run enterprises easily. Changes that occurred recently are:

A Flourishing Economy:

The UAE has a flourishing and stable economy with numerous opportunities to maximize your earning potential.

Geographical Prospects:

The UAE is situated between Asia and Europe, which makes it easier to access worldwide markets and makes it a global commercial hub.

Specialized and Skilled Talent:

Dubai has one of the most competent and diverse populations in the world. Businesses can hire skilled workers who have expertise and experience in a wide range of disciplines.

Unlimited Business Prospects:

In the UAE, you can choose from more than two thousand business activities that are part of various businesses and sectors.

Favorable Regimes for Female Entrepreneurs:

There are more supportive organizations, advice groups, and workshops for female entrepreneurs in the UAE. So, creating an open atmosphere while promoting an inclusive and diverse environment.

Cutting-Edge Infrastructure:

The nation’s cutting-edge infrastructure, including its power supply and telecommunications systems, is outstanding.

A Robust Financial System:

The financial system in the UAE is sturdy and safe. The system meets global requirements for openness, speed, and safety.

Support from the Government Authorities:

Dubai has favorable policies for startups, such as tax breaks, investment perks, and customs standards that are easy to follow.

Easy Currency Transfers:

There are no currency limits right now, which makes it easy to transfer money worldwide in any currency.

Maximize Global Direct Investment:

Foreign direct investment in the UAE has increased over the last years due to the maximization of foreign investment potential in the region. It is one of the best regions in the world to invest in, welcoming businesspeople from all over the world.

As these measures indicate, Dubai is dedicated to encouraging business development and foreign investment.

Essential Concerns to Open a Business in Dubai as a Foreigner

Before you start a business in Dubai, you need to know a few facts about how to open a business in Dubai as a foreigner. These regulations will also be the same for all registered businesses in the UAE. If you’re a foreigner and intend to start a business in Dubai, here are some things to bear in mind.

Determine the Type of Business:

The initial and most crucial thing to do is to set up the business and decide on the type and structure you intend it to be. It determines what kind of business you have and other things like how it runs and what its goals are.

Select Business Area:

In Dubai, you can register a business in two places: the mainland and free zones.

Dubai Mainland Business

A Mainland company is registered with the UAE’s DED and needs its permission to launch a business. If you intend to do business on the UAE’s Mainland, you must initially register a business with the DED. After that, you will receive a business license that will let you start operations in the UAE.

If you want to start a business in Dubai, you can conduct business with global and regional markets. One of the positive aspects of registering a business in Dubai’s mainland is that you can acquire your license in just one day.

Dubai Freezone Business:

Starting a business in a Dubai Free Zone can be more profitable and productive. It has the ideal conditions for starting a new business. Certain guidelines must be followed when starting a business in the free zone. However, there are also a lot of benefits for foreign entities that do so.

Get A Business License:

Opening a business in Dubai is not straightforward for someone from outside the country. Especially when you’re in a foreign nation, it takes extensive and careful planning to expand your business and run it smoothly. There are multiple types of business licenses in Dubai.

You need to get a license based on what your business needs. The DED issues the following categories of licenses:

  • License for industry.
  • License for business.
  • License for professionals.
  • License for craftsmanship.
  • License for agriculture.
  • License for tourism.

Exploring the Essential Phases for Opening a Business in Dubai as an Expat

How do you open a business in Dubai as a foreigner? These are the essential procedures you need to follow to register a business as an expat in Dubai.

Business Strategy for Action:

A beneficial business strategy includes essential phases. It’s hard to start a business in another country, as you don’t know the area or the restrictions. It is crucial to have a proper business approach that includes all the steps that need to be taken. You need to know more about the country in great detail. You can also get support from a partner in your area. It can also help you receive your clearances more quickly.

Business Visa and The Paperwork:

If you want to travel for business purposes, you need to apply for a business visa. Business visas also let high-level employees qualify for permanent residency. Non-resident business owners can get long-term visas for themselves and their families by corresponding with the embassy in their country.

You must have the following papers on hand to get through the immigration process:

  • Completed application form.
  • Initial authorization and documents
  • NOC from regional sponsor
  • Business strategy
  • Passport copies of business owners and partners with a minimum of six months’ validity.
  • Proof of residence of business owners
  • Signatures of appointed director and shareholders
  • Permissions from other government authorities
  • MOA
  • Attested copy of rental agreement.
  • Further paperwork requested by DED.

Getting The License:

Your business license is one of the most significant documents you need to form a company in Dubai. Based on the business category, you need to get various licenses from DLD.

Start your business in Dubai with ConnectFZ

Conclusion

This blog post talks about how to open a business in Dubai as a foreigner. Starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner or non-resident is an excellent option. The Emirate has a robust economy, premium geographic perks, and a favorable business climate. As a foreign entrepreneur, you can establish your firm in Dubai if you get the right advice and plan ahead.

Connect FZ Business Setup Consultants can help open a business in Dubai for a simplified and smooth procedure. Get in touch with us today.

title: Steps for Company Registration in UAE Free Zone: Guide
content:
Since free zones in the UAE have become popular, many foreign investors want to set up their companies there now. And if you are one of those investors, you must learn about the company registration in UAE free zone. This way, you’ll be able to learn how to set up your business and operate it as soon as possible.

In this article, you’ll learn everything that you should know about this registration process and the steps to complete it. Besides, here you will also find useful information about the business licenses, costs, benefits, and other elements regarding free zones. Furthermore, you can also get some tips to register your company more efficiently. Let’s observe:

  1. What is a free zone in the UAE and why should set up your company in one of them?
  2. How many benefits can you get by setting up your company in a free zone?
  3. Which free zones are available in the UAE for setting up your business?
  4. What are the steps you should follow to register your company in a free zone?
  5. What documents are necessary for completing the registration process in a UAE free zone?
  6. How many business licenses can you find in the UAE free zones?
  7. Learn about the cost of registering your company in a free zone in the UAE.
  8. Where else can you register your business in the UAE?
  9. How can Connectfz help you register your business in your chosen UAE free zone?
 
 

1. What is a free zone in the UAE and why should set up your company in one of them?

Free zones are special locations that investors choose to set up their companies or businesses and trade their products. In the UAE, they can find many different free zones to achieve their goals and make their businesses thrive. And if you want to do the same, you should learn how complete the company registration in UAE free zone.

Nonetheless, you should first learn about the reasons why investors like you choose these places as their business locations. And the main one is that they can boost their business by enjoying the different advantages of these trade zones. For example, they can trade their products or services at preferential tax and customs rates.

On the other hand, free zone companies in Dubai or any other emirate can have access to workers, facilities, and more. Furthermore, many specific free zones are also strategic locations for doing business internationally, which is convenient for many entrepreneurs. Keep reading below to find out more favorable elements that free zones in the UAE offer.

Discover some free zones in the UAE like Dubai Outsource Free Zone in which you can register your company.

2. How many benefits can you get by setting up your company in a free zone?

In case you decide to establish your company in a free zone in this country, you will get several benefits. For example, you can have 100 percent of your company ownership and enjoy multiple tax exemptions as well. Therefore, we should take a look at the most common advantages that all free zones offer to investors:

  • 100 percent of foreign ownership of your business.
  • Full exemption from several taxes, such as corporate and personal income tax.
  • There are no taxes on import and export duties either.
  • And there is also full repatriation of profits and capital.
  • Investors can also enjoy a favorable environment due to the business-friendly rules and regulations.
  • You can have access to world-class resources and infrastructure to boost your business, and also excellent customer support.
  • Also, it is possible to obtain hi-tech facilities to operate your company, including office space, warehouse space, and land availability.
  • You can choose between a variety of free zones, and each of them will offer you many other benefits.

Here you can learn about the correct procedure to complete the Visa change process in the United Arab Emirates.

3. Which free zones are available in the UAE for setting up your business?

There is a great variety of free zones that you can choose from, specifically 45 of them. Although they share a lot of common benefits, some of them may vary according to the location. Besides, the company registration in UAE free zone also varies depending on the free zone that the investor selects.

Some of the cheapest free zones in UAE that you can choose to set up your business are these:

  • International Free Zone Authority (IFZA).
  • Jebel Ali Free Zone Authority (JAFZA).
  • Ajman Media City Free Zone (AMCFZ).
  • Ras Al Khaimah Economic Zone (RAKEZ).
  • Khalifa Industrial Zone Abu Dhabi (KIZAD).

Each of them counts on a list of the thousands of companies that operate in those free zones. And you are free to choose to join any of them whenever you feel ready to set up your own company. For instance, you can join the Jebel Ali Free Zone companies list by setting up in this free zone.

If you want to find a cheap location, here you can compare some of the cheapest free zones in the UAE.

Learn More About : Know about the documents required for trade license renewal in Dubai

4. What are the steps you should follow to register your company in a free zone?

title: Full Tax Invoice Format UAE: Simplified vs. Full Guide
content:
The tax authority of the federation established rules for the tax invoice format UAE issued for goods and services. Additionally, it states when taxable services are supplied or at the time of issuing these invoices. Also, businesses must meet all guidelines for issuing the tax invoice to avoid legal inconveniences.

In this article, you will be able to find out which entity issues the tax invoice format in the Emirates and what the requirements are. Moreover, the importance of the said invoice and many details that will help you comply with this important tax requirement.

Who Should Issue a Tax Invoice UAE?

A UAE tax invoice is a document issued by a VAT-registered individual to the receiver. Likewise, this invoice leaves a record when you deliver some goods or services where you must pay taxes. Furthermore, the executive regulations according to Article 59 show the requirements for a tax invoice and when you must issue it.

Likewise, this invoice must include information such as the name of the supplier, tax registration number, and total amount, among others. Thus, later we will detail more about what the tax bill should contain.

When Should You Issue a Tax Invoice?

The tax invoice format UAE, according to the law, may be issued after 14 days from the date of provision of goods or services. In addition, taxable persons must comply with the conditions established in Article 59 of the Executive Regulation. Additionally, businesses must comply with several regulations related to issuing tax invoices in the UAE.

  • When a company makes any supply, it is obligatory to issue a tax invoice UAE. In addition, the business must issue it and deliver it to the recipient for goods that meet the conditions for this.
  • The issuance of simplified tax invoices does not require the issuing company to show the net value of the items. That is, it does not require you to show the amount without taxes on the invoice.
  • In the case of issuing complete invoices, companies must show both the tax value and the net value. However, they are not required to show the gross value of the transaction on the invoice.
  • Issuing the tax invoice format UAE in foreign currency requires the tax sample in dirhams (AED). Additionally, you must state the exchange rate used for the conversion in the transaction.

What to consider When Submitting a Tax Invoice

Concerning the supply, a special provision will apply to periodic payments or consecutive invoices for goods and services. In addition, the tax invoice format expressed in foreign currency will have the following content:

  • Amount of tax payable expressed in AED.
  • The exchange rate applied.

What are the Tax Invoice Requirements in UAE?

The tax notification must comply with a series of valid requirements by law. Below, you will see the tax invoice requirements UAE in detail:

  • Tax bill in a prominent place
  • The sequential number
  • The date of the invoice
  • Delivery time if it is different
  • Supplier name, address, and TRN
  • Name of the recipient, address, and TRN
  • Description of the goods or services delivered
  • The unit cost, the quantity supplied, the tax rates, and the cost to pay in AED
  • Amount of any discount allowed
  • The gross price payable in AED
  • Tax cost payable in AED
  • If applicable, the exchange rate applied
  • If applicable, a declaration regarding the reverse charge

New amendment on the date of issue of a tax invoice

The new modification on the date of issuance of the UAE tax invoice format came into force on January 1, 2023. Thus, the law says that the issuance of an invoice must be 14 days after the delivery of services or goods. In this case, it differs from the old law, when there were no time limits for issuing the tax invoice.

Importance of UAE Tax Bill Format

If you register your company under VAT, you must ensure that you have the tax invoice format UAE. In this case, the invoice will allow you, as a registrant, to deliver services or any goods that are subject to legal taxes. Your company must have the VAT invoice issued by the FTA to avoid fines and penalties.

In addition, you must know how to prepare the VAT invoice format UAE to present it to the authorities.

UAE VAT Invoice Format Types

There are 2 types of tax invoice format UAE allowed according to the Federal Tax Authority or FTA:

  • Simplified tax bill. They are simple VAT invoices issued for supplies for an amount less than AED 10,000. Moreover, these kinds of invoices are for retail companies and do not need a VAT number.
  • Detailed tax bill. These types of invoices are for companies that provide goods and services to another for an amount greater than AED 10,000. Therefore, the tax invoice must contain more details when you issue it.

What data must be included in a tax invoice format

The decree of the law for VAT in the Emirates establishes that the tax invoice format UAE must contain the following data:

  • Clear display of the word TAX BILL.
  • The name, tax registration number, and address of the registrant making the supply.
  • If you are a registrant: The name, address, and tax registration number of the recipient.
  • A unique number or sequential Tax Invoice number.
  • Date of issue.
  • If it is different from the date of issue of the tax invoice format UAE, you must submit the date of supply.
  • Goods or services provided.
  • For each good or service, the quantity or volume supplied, the unit cost, the Tax rate, and the cost payable expressed in AED.
  • Price of any discount you have offered.
  • The gross amount payable referred to in AED

Also, you must express the tax payment in AED according to the exchange rate that applies when the currency is different from that of the UAE. On the other hand, the tax invoice describes a sub-intro where the recipient of goods or services must declare tax. This declaration made by the recipient must show the tax and a reference according to the law decree.

Data to include in a simplified tax invoice

You can apply this simplified tax invoice format UAE if the recipient of the goods is not registered under VAT. Also, applies if the recipient is a tax registrant but with the consideration for the supply of AED 10,000 or less. Thus, for this type of tax invoice, the data to include is the following:

  • The term TAX INVOICE must be seen
  • Registrant data that makes the supply: name, address, and tax registration number
  • Date of issue of the invoice
  • Services or goods supplied in the transaction
  • The total consideration and the amount of tax collected

Additionally, as stipulated by the FTA, any supplier must comply with the aforementioned data expressed in the tax invoice. Otherwise, the provider or registrant must pay an administrative penalty for non-compliance with laws and regulations. Therefore, make sure you comply with these requirements to avoid these types of problems with the law.

In the same way, a client who received the goods and services that are subject to tax must request the invoice for consideration. This will verify the legality of the transaction made about all deliveries. In addition, this will protect you, if you are the recipient, from fraud, as it provides transparency in operations.

What are the exemptions from issuing a tax invoice in UAE?

The law by decree requires the issuance of UAE tax invoice format in all situations but there are exemptions. Hence, this exemption applies when the issuer making the delivery verifies that the delivery qualifies for 0% tax. Furthermore, there is a vast registry to establish the details of this type of delivery.

What currency should be used on UAE tax invoices?

The monetary amount expressed in the tax invoice format UAE must be converted into dirhams (AED). This is based on the exchange rate accepted by the UAE Central Bank on the date of supply negotiation. In this regard, the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates publishes the exchange rates available for this service.

Historical rates

The Central Bank published the historical rates by specifying that it will not be necessary to process invoices issued before May 17, 2018. Also, the authorities changed to dirhams the amounts in invoices issued between January 1 and May 16, 2018. Likewise, this should be done through a reliable source as long as it has been used consistently for this.

Companies must use these historical data if the supply date is before May 17, 2018. Likewise, all tax invoices issued after that year must apply to the changes made by the UAE Central Bank. Furthermore, this will be regardless of whether the emitter supplied the goods or services in advance or after the publication of the Bank.

Exchange rates not rounded

To not round off, the Central Bank of the Emirates establishes that the companies must use the full exchange rate concerning the tax bill. For this process, they will use the same number of decimal places published.

Publication schedule

In the United Arab Emirates, the Central Bank updates exchange rates daily starting at 6:00 p.m. on its website. However, it is completely acceptable if you use the rates published the day before.

Import of services: reverse charge element

If companies use services from suppliers that are outside the country, the tax invoice must be in the currency of the exporting country. Thus, companies must use the exchange rate of the Central Bank to cancel the investment obligations of the charge. In this case, it is to calculate the VAT obligation to pay.

Likewise, an unregistered foreign supplier cannot issue a tax invoice. In this case, the commercial invoice date is acceptable as the supply date.

Invoices for imported goods

All invoices for goods brought from abroad received in foreign currency the customs department must convert them to dirhams. Likewise, you must complete the VAT due for this import in box 6 of the VAT declaration. However, keep in mind that the exchange made by customs is not the same as that of Central Bank UAE.

In this case, the customs calculation will prevail for tax or VAT declaration purposes. Likewise, companies will not have to declare any adjustments due to the change using the tax return in box 7.

How Businesses Can Unregistered at Issuance of VAT Invoices

Legal and natural persons registered under the FTA or Federal Tax Authority may opt out of VAT through an online process. Also, the reasons why they can unsubscribe will be due to the following circumstances:

  • They can apply for VAT deregistration after registering with the FTA if their business did not exceed AED 187,500 in 12 months,
  • If your company stops making deliveries subject to tax, you must request a VAT reduction.

Voluntary VAT disclosure

You must make this disclosure through a form issued by the FTA. In it, companies and taxpayers will be able to inform the FTA about any changes, errors in refunds, omissions, or VAT declarations.

In the same way, the voluntary VAT declaration in the Emirates is a form that helps correct errors you have made. This is concerning a refund or filing your VAT return. Additionally, it will allow you to voluntarily disclose errors to avoid a penalty.

How Can You Avoid Errors on a Tax Bill?

Every registrant must provide truthful information in the UAE tax invoice format. Thus, you should not present it incomplete nor should it contain false information because you will have to face administrative sanctions.

Consequently, the tax invoice format UAE is very important if you have business setup in Dubai mainland and other freezones. This is because it is a requirement to market goods and services but you must follow the rules and requirements imposed by law to avoid fines.

If you need help regarding this topic, do not hesitate to contact us, because we are a group of certified professionals at your disposal.

Data to include in a simplified tax invoice

You can apply this simplified tax invoice format UAE if the recipient of the goods is not registered under VAT. Also, applies if the recipient is a tax registrant but with the consideration for the supply of AED 10,000 or less. Thus, for this type of tax invoice, the data to include is the following:

  • The term TAX INVOICE must be seen
  • Registrant data that makes the supply: name, address, and tax registration number
  • Date of issue of the invoice
  • Services or goods supplied in the transaction
  • The total consideration and the amount of tax collected

Additionally, as stipulated by the FTA, any supplier must comply with the aforementioned data expressed in the tax invoice. Otherwise, the provider or registrant must pay an administrative penalty for non-compliance with laws and regulations. Therefore, make sure you comply with these requirements to avoid these types of problems with the law.

In the same way, a client who received the goods and services that are subject to tax must request the invoice for consideration. This will verify the legality of the transaction made about all deliveries. In addition, this will protect you, if you are the recipient, from fraud, as it provides transparency in operations.

What are the exemptions from issuing a tax invoice in UAE?

The law by decree requires the issuance of UAE tax invoice format in all situations but there are exemptions. Hence, this exemption applies when the issuer making the delivery verifies that the delivery qualifies for 0% tax. Furthermore, there is a vast registry to establish the details of this type of delivery.

What currency should be used on UAE tax invoices?

The monetary amount expressed in the tax invoice format UAE must be converted into dirhams (AED). This is based on the exchange rate accepted by the UAE Central Bank on the date of supply negotiation. In this regard, the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates publishes the exchange rates available for this service.

Historical rates

The Central Bank published the historical rates by specifying that it will not be necessary to process invoices issued before May 17, 2018. Also, the authorities changed to dirhams the amounts in invoices issued between January 1 and May 16, 2018. Likewise, this should be done through a reliable source as long as it has been used consistently for this.

Companies must use these historical data if the supply date is before May 17, 2018. Likewise, all tax invoices issued after that year must apply to the changes made by the UAE Central Bank. Furthermore, this will be regardless of whether the emitter supplied the goods or services in advance or after the publication of the Bank.

Exchange rates not rounded

To not round off, the Central Bank of the Emirates establishes that the companies must use the full exchange rate concerning the tax bill. For this process, they will use the same number of decimal places published.

Publication schedule

In the United Arab Emirates, the Central Bank updates exchange rates daily starting at 6:00 p.m. on its website. However, it is completely acceptable if you use the rates published the day before.

Import of services: reverse charge element

If companies use services from suppliers that are outside the country, the tax invoice must be in the currency of the exporting country. Thus, companies must use the exchange rate of the Central Bank to cancel the investment obligations of the charge. In this case, it is to calculate the VAT obligation to pay.

Likewise, an unregistered foreign supplier cannot issue a tax invoice. In this case, the commercial invoice date is acceptable as the supply date.

Invoices for imported goods

All invoices for goods brought from abroad received in foreign currency the customs department must convert them to dirhams. Likewise, you must complete the VAT due for this import in box 6 of the VAT declaration. However, keep in mind that the exchange made by customs is not the same as that of Central Bank UAE.

In this case, the customs calculation will prevail for tax or VAT declaration purposes. Likewise, companies will not have to declare any adjustments due to the change using the tax return in box 7.

How Businesses Can Unregistered at Issuance of VAT Invoices

Legal and natural persons registered under the FTA or Federal Tax Authority may opt out of VAT through an online process. Also, the reasons why they can unsubscribe will be due to the following circumstances:

  • They can apply for VAT deregistration after registering with the FTA if their business did not exceed AED 187,500 in 12 months,
  • If your company stops making deliveries subject to tax, you must request a VAT reduction.

Voluntary VAT disclosure

You must make this disclosure through a form issued by the FTA. In it, companies and taxpayers will be able to inform the FTA about any changes, errors in refunds, omissions, or VAT declarations.

In the same way, the voluntary VAT declaration in the Emirates is a form that helps correct errors you have made. This is concerning a refund or filing your VAT return. Additionally, it will allow you to voluntarily disclose errors to avoid a penalty.

How Can You Avoid Errors on a Tax Bill?

Every registrant must provide truthful information in the UAE tax invoice format. Thus, you should not present it incomplete nor should it contain false information because you will have to face administrative sanctions.

Consequently, the tax invoice format UAE is very important if you have business setup in Dubai mainland and other freezones. This is because it is a requirement to market goods and services but you must follow the rules and requirements imposed by law to avoid fines.
